title: Hong Kong environmental authorities vow smoking crackdown at Shek Kwu Chau waste plant following fire probe
zh_title: 香港环保部门誓言在石鼓洲废物处理厂进行火灾调查后严厉打击吸烟行为
summary: 调查人员发现吸烟或焊接工作是上个月该地点发生火灾的罪魁祸首后，香港环保部门发誓要严厉打击石鼓洲人工岛上一座废物管理设施的吸烟行为。 2026 年 10 月 26 日，香港石鼓洲人工岛上的 I·PARK1 垃圾焚烧厂冒出黑烟。照片：goblin_under，来自 Threads。消防处（FSD）周二表示，已完成对火灾的调查，火灾迫使香港第一座废物处理厂暂时关闭。
content:
调查人员发现吸烟或焊接工作是上个月该地点发生火灾的罪魁祸首后，香港环保部门发誓要严厉打击石鼓洲人工岛上一座废物管理设施的吸烟行为。 2026 年 10 月 26 日，香港石鼓洲人工岛上的 I·PARK1 垃圾焚烧厂冒出黑烟。照片：goblin_under，来自 Threads。消防处周二表示，已完成对10月26日香港首个垃圾焚烧炉的火灾调查，并疏散I·PARK1设施中近千人。调查人员在现场收集证据并听取相关人士的陈述后，“排除了电气故障、纵火和化学物质自燃等起火原因，怀疑与焊接有关”工作或吸烟，”FSD 说。环境保护署（环保署）回应称，已指示该设施的承建商立即检讨和加强防火措施，并全面实施禁烟令。 2026 年 10 月 26 日，香港石鼓洲人工岛上的 I·PARK1 垃圾焚烧厂冒出黑烟。照片：edward.chung_，来自 Threads。
环保署表示，自今年一月起，承建商已实施一系列控烟措施，包括要求工人在前往人工岛前在码头存放香烟和打火机，以及进行定期和突击巡查。工人在工地发现吸烟，会立即被勒令离开。上述调查结果是在对宏福苑火灾进行全面调查后发现，现场吸烟也是该住宅区经常出现的问题。去年发生导致168人死亡的大火时，该住宅区正在进行翻修。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong environmental authorities have vowed to crack down on smoking at a waste-management facility on an artificial island off Shek Kwu Chau, after investigators found that smoking or welding work was to blame for the blaze that broke out at the site last month. Black smoke rises from I·PARK1, a waste incineration plant on an artificial island off Shek Kwu Chau in Hong Kong on October 26, 2026. Photo: goblin_under, via Threads. The Fire Services Department (FSD) said on Tuesday it had completed its investigation into the fire, which forced the temporary shutdown of Hong Kong’s first waste-to-energy incinerator and the evacuation of close to 1,000 people from the I·PARK1 facility on October 26. After collecting evidence from the scene and taking statements from relevant parties, investigators “ruled out electrical faults, arson, and spontaneous combustion of chemical substances as the cause of the fire, which is instead suspected of being related to welding works or smoking,” the FSD said. In response , the Environmental Protection Department (EPD) said it had instructed the facility’s contractor to immediately review and strengthen its fire hazard mitigation measures and to enforce a comprehensive smoking ban. Black smoke rises from I·PARK1, a waste incineration plant on an artificial island off Shek Kwu Chau in Hong Kong on October 26, 2026. Photo: edward.chung_, via Threads. Since January this year, the EPD said, the contractor had implemented a series of smoking control measures, such as requiring workers to store cigarettes and lighters at the pier before transiting to the artificial island and conducting regular and surprise inspections. Workers found smoking on the construction site were immediately ordered to leave, the department said. The findings come after a comprehensive investigation into the Wang Fuk Court fire found that on-site smoking was also a recurring issue at the housing estate, which was undergoing renovations when the inferno that killed 168 people broke out last year.

title: Singapore in damage control after Nvidia scandal exposes China loophole

content:
新加坡正在努力维护其作为值得信赖的商业中心的声誉，但有指控称，中国公司尽管受到美国出口限制，却利用新加坡获取高端人工智能芯片。新加坡。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。不久前担任美国芯片巨头英伟达(Nvidia)总裁的黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)与一名涉嫌中国间谍之间的风流韵事引发了一场不断扩大的丑闻，凸显了这个城市国家作为人工智能驱动的先进半导体全球十字路口的地位。美国周一采取行动，堵住了向中国出口强大人工智能芯片的控制漏洞，称此举是为了保护国家安全。美国新规定不仅打击非法芯片走私，还打击中国公司从第三国（通常位于东南亚）装满先进英伟达芯片的数据中心租用计算能力的巨大灰色市场。在此之前，黄与新加坡云计算公司 Megaspeed International 前高管 Alice Huang 的恋情爆发了爆炸性报道，华盛顿正在调查该公司涉嫌规避美国规定将 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国的行为。新加坡国立大学政治学家庄家彦告诉法新社，这一丑闻“显然对新加坡来说不是什么好事”。新加坡也在调查 Megaspeed 的所作所为，但 Chong 表示，新加坡必须加强监管，以避免给人留下“系统性问题”的印象。 Nvidia 的 H200 芯片。
照片：英伟达。他表示，英伟达案可能会让“通过简单地处理个别案件而不是制定更严格的法规和法律来维持作为廉洁商业中心的声誉”变得更加困难。据报道，一些美国官员还认为，与穿着皮夹克的詹森没有关系的爱丽丝·黄正在为北京从事间谍活动。陷入交火？新加坡表示，正在仔细研究美国的新措施，该措施要求全球数据中心持有美国许可证，才能向总部位于中国或美国武器禁运其他地区的公司提供来自先进芯片的大量计算能力。向新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西运送先进芯片还需要获得美国许可证，美国商务部表示这些国家的敏感组件存在“高于正常的转移风险”。 “我们非常重视我们的国际声誉，”新加坡政府表示。声明称，新加坡不会“纵容企业利用与新加坡的联系，在国际商业活动中规避或违反其他国家的法律，包括出口管制”。一些分析师表示，新加坡正在努力应对很大程度上超出其控制范围的因素，并陷入美中科技竞争的交火中。 Nvidia 总部位于加利福尼亚州圣克拉拉。照片：英伟达。
英伟达控制着用于训练和运行人工智能模型的芯片市场的约 90%，华盛顿从四年前就开始限制其对中国的销售。新加坡风险咨询公司亚太经济研究所 (Asia-Pacific Economics) 负责人拉吉夫·比斯瓦斯 (Rajiv Biswas) 表示，“此类出口管制的责任主要应由政府负责”，而不是“将执法工作外包给其他司法管辖区”。 “在此前的多起企业利用新加坡作为受限制高科技人工智能芯片转运点的案件中，新加坡已经采取了强有力的执法措施。” “门户开放政策”

【原文 English Original】
Singapore is working to maintain its reputation as a trusted business hub, tainted by allegations that Chinese companies had exploited it to gain access to top-end AI chips despite US export restrictions. Singapore. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. A widening scandal sparked by an affair between Jensen Huang, until recently head of US chip titan Nvidia, and a suspected Chinese spy has spotlighted the city-state’s position as a global crossroads for the advanced semiconductors that power artificial intelligence. The United States on Monday moved to close a loophole in its controls — which it says protect national security — on the export of powerful AI chips to China. The new US rules crack down on illicit chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres full of advanced Nvidia chips in third countries, often in Southeast Asia. It follows explosive reports of Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, which Washington is investigating for the alleged transfer of Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of US rules. The scandal “is obviously not a good look for Singapore”, Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist with the National University of Singapore, told AFP. Singapore is also probing what Megaspeed was up to, but Chong said the city-state must strengthen regulatory oversight to avoid the perception of “systemic issues”. Nvidia’s H200 chips. Photo: Nvidia. The Nvidia case may make it harder “to maintain the reputation of being a clean business hub by simply dealing with individual cases, rather than putting more stringent regulations and laws in place”, he said. Some US officials also reportedly believe that Alice Huang, no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen, was spying for Beijing. Caught in crossfire? Singapore said it was carefully studying the new US measures, which require data centres worldwide to hold a US licence to provide a large volume of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, or other places under US arms embargoes. A US licence will also be needed to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US commerce department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the sensitive components. “We take our international reputation seriously,” the Singaporean government said. The city-state does not “condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate the laws of other countries in their international business activities, including export controls”, it said. Some analysts said Singapore was grappling with factors largely beyond its control, caught in the crossfire of US-China tech rivalry. Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California. Photo: Nvidia. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for chips used to train and run AI models, and Washington began restricting their sales to China four years ago. “The responsibility for such export controls should primarily rest with the government issuing” them, “rather than outsourcing enforcement of laws to other jurisdictions”, said Rajiv Biswas, chief of the risk consultancy Asia-Pacific Economics in Singapore. “Singapore has already been taking strong enforcement measures in a number of previous cases where companies have used Singapore as a transhipment point for restricted high-tech AI chips.” ‘Open-door policy’ Megaspeed — which before 2023 operated under a different name as an arm of a Chinese video game developer — reportedly traded in upwards of $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips over just two years. A financial trail weaving through Singapore, Malaysia and the Cayman Islands suggests Megaspeed’s business may have been boosted by a connection to Chinese tech giant Alibaba. Singapore has positioned itself as a “critical node” in the global semiconductor supply chain — attracting more than $23 billion in investments between 2022-25. The city accounted for “one in 10 chips and one in five semiconductor equipment units worldwide”, its economic development board says. Singapore is seeking to attract further investment from tech giants, but its vulnerabilities to global business flashpoints have been underscored as a small, open economy. Singapore. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at tech research firm Omdia, described the Megaspeed scandal as an “isolated controversy” borne of various factors, including a recent change of guard in the United States following midterm elections. Singapore “will continue to be exposed to controversies like this due to its open-door policy when it comes to trade and commerce”, he told AFP. “I believe the government will do whatever it can to exert more regulatory oversight.”

title: District official proposes ride-hail pickup zone at Kai Tak to curb illegal cross-border rides
zh_title: 地区官员提议在启德设立网约车接送区以遏制非法跨境乘车
summary: 在中国游客非法乘车返回大陆后，一名区级官员建议在该市旗舰体育场外设立专门的有牌照车辆接送区。香港启德体育公园。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周五，韩国男团BIGBANG在启德体育场演出时，中国内地游客选择无牌出租汽车越过边境回家，九龙城区议员张敬勋周二就香港电台的一档节目提出了这一建议。然而，由于车辆绕道，游客很难上车
content:
在中国游客非法乘车返回大陆后，一名区级官员建议在该市旗舰体育场外设立专门的有牌照车辆接送区。香港启德体育公园。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周五，韩国男团BIGBANG在启德体育场演出时，中国内地游客选择无牌出租汽车越过边境回家，九龙城区议员张敬勋周二就香港电台的一档节目提出了这一建议。然而，游客们很难上车，因为车辆绕道避开音乐会场地周围设立的警察检查站。出租汽车甚至在附近的住宅区启恩苑外的环岛接载乘客，音乐会观众挤满了住宅区的入口。张周二表示，为拥有在该市提供服务的许可的网约车设立专门的接送区域，将抑制游客雇用无证乘车服务。新制度“一旦他们意识到必须走得更远才能登机，他们就会失去雇用他们的动力，”张说。由于没有专门的监管，优步等叫车服务多年来一直在合法的灰色地带运营。今年 8 月，香港开始接受网约车司机和平台的申请，首批 10,000 个许可证允许他们合法运营。
张表示，新制度实施后，游客可乘坐香港牌照的出租车到口岸，然后转乘内地出租车。 跨境网约车被称为“白牌”车辆，在香港是非法的。警察局长周乔恩上周表示，警方逮捕了 12 名涉嫌提供非法跨境服务的司机，其中包括在 BIGBANG 演唱会期间提供服务的司机。张表示，警方的行动将帮助内地司机了解他们的行为是违法的，同时帮助游客为未来的行程做好准备。他补充说，体育场附近的停车场或其他空地可以用作叫车接送站。

【原文 English Original】
A district-level official has suggested setting up a dedicated ride-hail pickup area for licensed vehicles outside the city’s flagship stadium after Chinese tourists hired illicit rides back to the mainland. Hong Kong’s Kai Tak Sports Park. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Kowloon City District Councillor Cheung King-fan made the suggestion on an RTHK programme on Tuesday after mainland Chinese tourists opted for unlicensed hire cars back home across the border on Friday, when South Korean boyband BIGBANG performed at Kai Tak Stadium. The tourists struggled to board, however, as the vehicles took detours to avoid police checkpoints set up around the concert venue. Hire cars even picked up passengers at the roundabout outside Kai Yan Court, a nearby housing estate, with concertgoers crowding out the entrance to the housing block. Cheung said on Tuesday that setting up a dedicated pickup area for ride-hail vehicles with permits to provide services in the city would disincentivise tourists from hiring unlicensed rides. New regime “Once they realise they have to walk further away to board, they will lose the incentive to hire them,” Cheung said. With no dedicated regulation, ride-hail services such as Uber have operated in a legal grey area for years. Hong Kong began accepting applications for ride-hail drivers and platforms this August for an initial pool of 10,000 permits allowing them to operate legally. Cheung said that once the new regime took effect, tourists would be able to take Hong Kong-licensed hire cars to boundary control points and then transfer to mainland hire vehicles. Cross-border ride-hail cars, known as “white licence” vehicles, are illegal in Hong Kong. Police chief Joe Chow said last week that the force had arrested 12 drivers suspected of providing illegal cross-border services, including at the BIGBANG concert. Cheung said the police operation would help mainland drivers understand that their actions were illegal while helping tourists prepare for their trips in the future. He added that a parking lot or other empty sites near the stadium could be used as a ride-hail pickup stand.

title: Hong Kong records 14,000 cybersecurity incidents in first 10 months of 2026 as lawmaker urges tougher penalties
zh_title: 香港2026年前10个月共发生14,000起网络安全事件，立法会议员敦促加强处罚
summary: 今年前 10 个月，香港已记录约 14,000 起网络安全事件，同比增长 7%，一名立法者认为，更严厉的处罚将迫使企业加强对其系统和客户数据的防御。面对人工智能的快速发展，网络安全正成为许多公司日益关注的问题。资料照片：Pexels。这些数据来自香港计算机应急小组协调中心，该中心隶属于香港生产力促进局，负责协调对网络威胁的响应。近几个月来，高收益
content:
今年前 10 个月，香港已记录约 14,000 起网络安全事件，同比增长 7%，一名立法者认为，更严厉的处罚将迫使企业加强对其系统和客户数据的防御。面对人工智能的快速发展，网络安全正成为许多公司日益关注的问题。资料照片：Pexels。这些数据来自香港计算机应急小组协调中心，该中心隶属于香港生产力促进局，负责协调对网络威胁的响应。近几个月来，香港航空、国泰航空和崇光百货等公司遭遇了备受瞩目的数据泄露事件。立法会议员吴约翰尼周二在电台节目中表示，鉴于最近发生的一系列网络安全事件，需要审查《个人资料（隐私）条例》。他建议修改立法，要求公司在规定的时间内向当局报告数据泄露事件，并加大对未能这样做的处罚力度。 “对于非关键基础设施公司来说，如果他们的客户群有一定规模，我认为应该有一个固定和指定的时间来报告[网络安全事件]，”吴用粤语说。 “这让客户有时间保护自己。” “另一方面……如果有惩罚，公司自然会投入更多资源来降低数据被盗的可能性，”他补充道。
吴说，政府可以为企业提供技术和财政支持，以提升其网络安全能力。他还认为，生产力委员会应该向网络安全协调中心分配更多人力，并指出该委员会目前有25名网络安全专家，其中约一半在该中心工作。应对人工智能威胁立法者 Ray Wong 在同一广播节目中表示，最近大约一半的网络安全事件与网络钓鱼有关，这是一种网络攻击，黑客冒充可信实体窃取敏感信息。黄说，这一激增可能是由于公司的网络安全措施落后于人工智能的快速发展。生产力委员会表示，其专家已部署人工智能来应对人工智能驱动的网络威胁。 2026 年 5 月 21 日，香港生产力促进局在九龙塘举办的人工智能展览。资料图片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。黄敦促公司执行更严格的网络安全协议，例如定期更新其安全系统和数据库密码。但他反对为公司报告数据泄露设定具体的时间表，称此类事件需要调查，过早披露可能会引发不必要的恐慌。
“我认为政府在决定立法机制时，应该考虑这些方面，给企业时间进行调查，同时确保公众的知情权，”他用粤语说。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong has recorded about 14,000 cybersecurity incidents in the first 10 months of this year, a seven per cent year-on-year increase, as a lawmaker argued that tougher penalties would compel companies to strengthen defences for their systems and customer data. Cybersecurity is becoming a growing concern for many companies in the face of rapid advances in AI. File photo: Pexels. The figures came from the Hong Kong Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre, which operates under the Hong Kong Productivity Council to coordinate responses to cyber threats. In recent months, high-profile data breaches have hit companies such as Hong Kong Airlines, Cathay Pacific and department store SOGO. Speaking on a radio programme on Tuesday, lawmaker Johnny Ng said the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance needed to be reviewed in light of the recent string of cybersecurity incidents. He suggested amending the legislation to require firms to report data breaches to authorities within a specified timeframe and increase penalties for failing to do so. “For non-critical infrastructure firms, if their customer base is of a certain scale, I think there should be a fixed and specified timeframe to report [cybersecurity incidents],” Ng said in Cantonese. “This gives customers time to protect themselves.” “On the other hand… if there are penalties, companies will naturally invest more resources to make their data less likely to be stolen,” he added. The government could provide technical and financial support for firms to upgrade their cybersecurity capacity, Ng said. He also argued that the Productivity Council should allocate more manpower to the cybersecurity coordination centre, noting that the council currently has 25 cybersecurity experts, about half of whom work at the centre. Countering AI threats Speaking on the same radio programme, lawmaker Ray Wong said that roughly half of the recent cybersecurity incidents were related to phishing – a type of cyberattack in which hackers pose as trusted entities to steal sensitive information. The surge could be attributed to companies’ cybersecurity measures being outpaced by rapid advances in AI, Wong said. The Productivity Council has said that its experts have deployed AI to counter AI-enabled cyber threats. The Hong Kong Productivity Council’s AI exhibition in Kowloon Tong on May 21, 2026. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wong urged firms to enforce stricter cybersecurity protocols, such as regularly updating their security systems and database passwords. But he argued against setting up a specified timeframe for companies to report data leaks, saying that such incidents required investigation and that premature disclosure could trigger unnecessary panic. “I think that when the government decides on the legislative mechanism, it should consider these aspects and give companies time to conduct investigations, and at the same time ensure the public’s right to know,” he said in Cantonese.

title: Civil servants ‘do not mind’ working off-hours when required, official says, ruling out ‘right to disconnect’ law
zh_title: 官员表示，公务员“不介意”在需要时加班，排除了“断线权”法律
summary: 在一名议员询问香港是否会考虑为政府雇员实施“断线权”法律后，一名香港官员表示，公务员不介意在周末工作。公务员事务局局长杨颖于2023年12月14日向记者发表讲话。图片：香港政府一站通。公务员事务局局长杨英慧在周一的立法会会议上表示，政府范围内的动员协议要求公务员在紧急情况下，包括周六和周日，必须在场。 “如果他们断开连接，[我们将]无法
content:
在一名议员询问香港是否会考虑为政府雇员实施“断线权”法律后，一名香港官员表示，公务员不介意在周末工作。公务员事务局局长杨颖于2023年12月14日向记者发表讲话。图片：香港政府一站通。公务员事务局局长杨英慧在周一的立法会会议上表示，政府范围内的动员协议要求公务员在紧急情况下，包括周六和周日，必须在场。 “如果他们断开连接，[我们将]无法联系到他们。[我们将]无法动员尽可能多的同事，”杨用粤语告诉公共服务委员会。她的评论是对立法者叶克里斯（Chris Ip）的回应，叶克里斯表示，他观察到越来越多的国家采用了断开法律的权利。 “下班后，他们有权不回复短信和电话，”叶用粤语说。立法会议员叶克里斯.照片：Chris Ip，来自 Facebook。 “我知道公务员非常负责任，下班后不介意接受上级的提问或要求，”民建联成员叶说。 “但是政府会考虑在未来的家庭友好政策中增加脱离法律的权利吗？”他问道。家庭护理假杨提到的政府范围内的动员协议于 2022 年首次宣布。
当局表示，该协议旨在提高治理和应急响应能力。在会议上，杨补充说，主管只会在紧急情况下联系下属，并表示“否则会影响士气”。会议期间，杨还讨论了一项新举措，给予政府雇员最多 12 小时的带薪家庭护理年假。香港公务员。资料图片：香港政府一站通。根据新举措，员工每次可以请一到四个小时的假期来处理家庭事务，例如陪同亲戚去看医生和参加孩子学校的活动。杨表示，处理宠物相关事宜并不算请假理由。立法会议员林伟江询问政府会否考虑将休假时数从12小时增加至24小时，并指出部分雇员可能会请假带年长亲属去看病，而轮候时间可能会很长。对此，杨女士表示，她认为 12 小时是“合适的”，如果员工需要离开更长时间，可以休息半天。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong official has said civil servants do not mind working on weekends when called upon, after a lawmaker asked if the city would consider implementing a “right to disconnect” law for government employees. Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung speaks to reporters on December 14, 2023. Photo: GovHK. Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung said during a Legislative Council meeting on Monday that the government-wide mobilisation protocol required civil servants to be available during emergencies, including on Saturdays and Sundays. “If they disconnect, [we wouldn’t] be able to reach them. [We wouldn’t] be able to mobilise as many colleagues,” Yeung told the Panel on Public Service in Cantonese. Her comments were in response to lawmaker Chris Ip, who said he had observed more countries adopting right to disconnect laws. “After work, they have the right not to [respond to] messages and phone calls,” Ip said in Cantonese. Lawmaker Chris Ip. Photo: Chris Ip, via Facebook. “I know civil servants are very responsible, and do not mind taking questions or requests from their supervisors after work,” Ip, a member of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong, said. “But will the government consider adding right to disconnect laws to future family-friendly policies?” he asked. Family care leave The government-wide mobilisation protocol Yeung referred to was first announced in 2022. Authorities have said that the protocol is aimed at improving governance and emergency response capabilities. During the meeting, Yeung added that supervisors would only contact their subordinates when something was urgent, saying “otherwise, it would affect morale.” Also during the meeting, Yeung discussed a new initiative granting government employees up to 12 hours of paid annual family care leave . Hong Kong civil servants. File photo: GovHK. Under the new initiative, employees can take between one and four hours’ leave each time to attend to family matters such as accompanying relatives to medical appointments and attending events at their children’s schools. Yeung said that handling matters related to pets would not count as a reason for taking the leave. Lawmaker Lam Wai-kong asked whether the government would consider increasing the number of leave hours from 12 to 24, noting that some employees might take leave to bring elderly relatives to medical appointments where wait times could be long. In response, Yeung said she believed 12 hours was “appropriate” and that employees could take a half-day off if they needed to be away for a longer period.

title: Cold front to bring 15°C lows to Hong Kong on Friday, rain next week
zh_title: 冷锋周五为本港带来摄氏15度低温 下周有雨
summary: 临近周末，香港将迎来另一场寒流，天文台预计本周五最低气温将达到 15 摄氏度。资料图片：香港政府一站通。气象部门预计周四最低气温为 18 摄氏度，周五气温为 15 至 18 摄氏度。天文台表示，一股冷锋将于周三起横过中国南部沿海：“北风将增强，该地区将有几阵雨，气温将明显下降。在强烈的东北季风和雨云带的影响下，
content:
临近周末，香港将迎来另一场寒流，天文台预计本周五最低气温将达到 15 摄氏度。资料图片：香港政府一站通。气象部门预计周四最低气温为 18 摄氏度，周五气温为 15 至 18 摄氏度。天文台表示，周三起一股冷锋将横过中国南部沿海：“北风将增强，局部地区有小雨，气温将明显下降。受东北季候风及雨云影响，本周后半段广东天气普遍凉爽。”然而，周末后半段气温将再次上升，预计下周中旬将有阵雨。有记录以来最热的十月 天文台录得有史以来最高的十月月平均最高气温30.5摄氏度后，本月第二次寒潮来临。本月早些时候，该机构在一份新闻稿中表示：“主要是由于东北季风较正常弱，华南地区高空反气旋较正常强，加上气候变暖和可能持续到明年初的强烈厄尔尼诺现象，导致2026年10月香港异常温暖。”
政府间气候变化专门委员会警告说，自 20 世纪 50 年代以来，由于人为造成的气候变化，热浪的强度和频率持续增加。二氧化碳等温室气体的盛行（将热量滞留在大气中）提高了地球表面温度，更热、更长时间的热浪将生命置于危险之中。另请参阅：极端高温如何成为世界天气灾害中最致命的无声杀手 研究非政府组织伯克利地球表示，自工业革命以来，香港的气温已经升高了 1.7 摄氏度。根据 2023 年的一项研究，到本世纪末，高温和湿度可能会在较长时间内达到致命水平，导致世界某些地区无法呆在户外。

【原文 English Original】
Hongkongers will experience another cold snap towards the weekend, with the Observatory predicting lows of 15 degrees Celsius this Friday. File Photo: GovHK. The weather service expects lows of 18 degrees Celsius on Thursday, with temperatures on Friday ranging from 15 to 18 degrees Celsius. A cold front will cross China’s southern coast from Wednesday, the Observatory said: “Winds will strengthen from the north and there will be a few rain patches over the region. Temperatures will fall appreciably. Under the influence of the associated intense northeast monsoon and a band of rain and clouds, the weather will be generally cool over Guangdong in the latter part of this week.” However, temperatures will rise again during the latter part of the weekend, with showers expected by the middle of next week. Hottest October on record The second cold snap of the month comes after the Observatory recorded the highest-ever October monthly mean maximum temperature of 30.5 degrees Celsius. “Mainly due to a weaker-than-normal northeast monsoon and a stronger-than-normal upper-air anticyclone over southern China, and set against the backdrop of climate warming and a very strong El Niño event that may persist into early next year, October 2026 was unseasonably warm in Hong Kong,” it said earlier this month in a press release. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change has warned that the intensity and frequency of heatwaves have continued to increase since the 1950s due to human-caused climate change. The prevalence of greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide – which trap heat in the atmosphere – raises the planet’s surface temperature, with hotter, longer heatwaves putting lives at risk. See also: How extreme heat became the deadliest silent killer among world weather disasters Hong Kong has already warmed by 1.7 degrees Celsius since the Industrial Revolution, research NGO Berkeley Earth says . Heat and humidity may reach lethal levels for protracted periods by the end of the century, according to a 2023 study , making it impossible to stay outdoors in some parts of the world.

title: Hong Kong privacy watchdog launches compliance check over facial recognition system at Lam Tin estate
zh_title: 香港隐私监管机构对蓝田村的面部识别系统进行合规检查
summary: 香港隐私监管机构对一家物业管理公司在住宅区实施面部识别系统的计划启动了合规检查，此前该计划引起了居民的隐私担忧。 2020 年 11 月的拉古纳市。照片：Wikimedia Commons。当地媒体报道蓝田丽港城物业管理公司将推出面部识别门禁系统后，个人资料私隐专员公署（公署）于上周五发表上述声明。该公司 Citybase Property Management 周一回复当地媒体称
content:
香港隐私监管机构对一家物业管理公司在住宅区实施面部识别系统的计划启动了合规检查，此前该计划引起了居民的隐私担忧。 2020 年 11 月的拉古纳市。照片：Wikimedia Commons。当地媒体报道蓝田丽港城物业管理公司将推出面部识别门禁系统后，个人资料私隐专员公署（公署）于上周五发表上述声明。 Citybase Property Management公司周一回复当地媒体称，将配合监管机构的合规审计，并将根据该市的隐私法处理居民的生物识别数据。它还表示，新系统目前正在该小区四期中的三期安装，将提高居民的便利性并优化管理服务。 “敏感个人数据” 监管机构周五指出，“面部图像构成敏感个人数据”，该庄园可能涉及 8,000 多个家庭。公署表示，已主动对相关系统展开合规检查，以确保有关居民的个人资料得到充分保障。
另请参阅：香港警方在人工智能闭路电视网络上启动面部识别，警长表示工具“不会被滥用”。“公署已要求该公司提供进一步信息，以确保其遵守《个人资料（隐私）条例》和相关数据保护原则。”审计将审查在收集、持有、处理或使用居民生物识别数据时如何确保数据安全。个人资料私隐专员办公室。资料照片：Peter Lee/HKFP。监管机构还告诉居民，如果怀疑自己的个人资料隐私受到侵犯，可以向物业管理公司查询或向公署投诉。观塘区议员邓永俊在香港电台节目中表示，他收到了支持和反对面部识别推广的反馈，一些老年居民认为新系统会带来更多便利，而另一些居民则表达了隐私方面的担忧。他表示，新系统定于一月份投入使用，并计划在年底举行信息发布会。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong’s privacy watchdog has launched a compliance check into a property management firm’s plan to implement a facial recognition system at a residential estate after the initiative raised privacy concerns among residents. Laguna City in November 2020. Photo: Wikimedia Commons. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD) issued the statement last Friday, after local media reported that the estate management firm at Laguna City in Lam Tin would roll out a facial recognition access system. The firm, Citybase Property Management, replied to local media on Monday saying that it would cooperate with the watchdog’s compliance audit and that residents’ biometric data would be handled in accordance with the city’s privacy laws. It also said that the new system, currently being installed at three of the estate’s four phases, would improve convenience for residents and optimise management services. ‘Sensitive personal data’ The watchdog on Friday noted that “facial images constitute sensitive personal data” and that there may be over 8,000 households involved at the estate. “The PCPD has proactively commenced a compliance check on the relevant system to ensure that the personal data of the residents concerned is adequately protected,” it said. See also: Hong Kong police activate facial recognition across AI-enabled CCTV network, as police chief says tools ‘won’t be abused’ “The PCPD has requested further information from the Company to make sure that it complies with the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance and the relevant data protection principles,” it said. The audit will examine how data security is ensured in the collection, holding, processing or use of residents’ biometric data. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data. File photo: Peter Lee/HKFP. The watchdog also told residents to make enquiries with the property management firm or file a complaint to the PCPD if they suspected that their personal data privacy had been infringed. Speaking on an RTHK programme, Kwun Tong District Councillor Tang Wing-chun said that he had received feedback both for and against the facial recognition push, with some elderly residents believing the new system would bring more convenience, and others voicing privacy concerns. He said that the new system was set to go live in January, with an information session planned towards the end of the year.

title: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ at Shenzhen summit
zh_title: 中国称习近平、特朗普和普京将在深圳峰会讨论“世界和平”
summary: 北京周一表示，中国、俄罗斯和美国领导人本周在深圳举行首次三边峰会时将讨论“世界和平”。中国国家主席习近平、美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。照片：法新社。习近平主席、唐纳德·特朗普和弗拉基米尔·普京将于周四在亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会期间在中国南方城市举行会晤。特朗普周一告诉记者，他还可能在中国会见朝鲜领导人金正恩，他说：“他可能会来，我不知道。那”
content:
北京周一表示，中国、俄罗斯和美国领导人本周在深圳举行首次三边峰会时将讨论“世界和平”。中国国家主席习近平、美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。照片：法新社。习近平主席、唐纳德·特朗普和弗拉基米尔·普京将于周四在亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会期间在中国南方城市举行会晤。特朗普周一告诉记者，他还可能在中国会见朝鲜领导人金正恩，他说：“他可能会来，我不知道。这取决于习主席。”中国没有透露三位领导人将讨论什么细节，但表示他们将“就维护世界和平、促进大国关系战略稳定进行深入交流”。 “这将具有开创性的意义，”外交部发言人毛宁周一在北京证实此次会面几小时后的新闻发布会上说。特朗普表示，领导人将讨论无核化的“棘手话题”，以及伊朗和乌克兰的战争。 “我们都会谈论经济和贸易，”他在离开白宫时补充道。克里姆林宫表示“这次会议的意义和象征意义怎么估计都不过分”。无核化 华盛顿不喜欢中国迅速扩张的核武库，并表示希望北京成为核军控协议的一部分。
然而，北京长期以来一直坚持认为，美国和俄罗斯应该先削减其庞大的核武库，然后才同意就自己的核武库进行谈判。美俄双边核武器条约二月份到期后，特朗普呼吁达成一项包括中国在内的“更好的协议”。北京当时拒绝加入裁军谈判。但美国国务院表示，在本周的一次通话中，中国最高外交官王毅和美国国务卿卢比奥“一致认为，进行有意义的领导人级别对话对于推进和平与无核化等目标的重要性”。 2025 年 7 月 11 日，中国外交部长王毅在马来西亚吉隆坡会见美国国务卿马可·卢比奥。图片：外交部。 “我们将讨论无核化——这是一个棘手的话题，因为我们中的任何人都很难说我们会摆脱核武器，对吧？”特朗普周一告诉记者。联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯表示，如果三位领导人“真正致力于实现有意义的无核化，这将是世界的一项伟大成就”。古特雷斯在菲律宾举行的东盟峰会上表示：“我们长期以来……一直在讨论和要求核领域裁军的必要性，我们相信，只有完全（没有）核武器，我们才会完全安全。”伊朗 特朗普表示，三位领导人也可能会讨论他在伊朗的战争。 “我们将讨论无核化。
特朗普周一对记者表示：“我们会谈论伊朗。我们的伊朗状况非常好，但我们会稍微谈谈伊朗。”特朗普周一对记者表示。作为伊朗的最大经济伙伴，中国长期以来一直寻求调解美以袭击德黑兰引发的冲突。这场长达数月的危机扰乱了全球航运，导致全球油价飙升。特朗普在10月下旬表示，美国已经消灭了伊朗的大部分军队，但仍然需要“照顾”其中一个或多个国家。与此同时，中国表示，避免重新爆发敌对行动是“首要任务”，并已在研究中。

【原文 English Original】
The leaders of China, Russia and the United States will discuss “world peace” when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week, Beijing said on Monday. Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Photo: AFP. Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are due to meet in the southern Chinese city on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Trump told reporters on Monday he could also meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, saying: “He may come, I don’t know. That’s up to President Xi.” China has provided few details as to what the three leaders will discuss but said they would hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”. “It will be of ground-breaking significance,” foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a news briefing on Monday, hours after Beijing confirmed the meeting. Trump said the leaders would discuss the “tough subject” of denuclearisation, as well as the wars in Iran and Ukraine. “We’ll all be talking about economics and trade,” he added as he left the White House. The Kremlin said “the significance and symbolism of this meeting are hard to overestimate”. Denuclearisation Washington, which dislikes China’s rapidly expanding nuclear arsenal, said it wants Beijing to be part of a nuclear arms control deal. Beijing, however, has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile. After a US-Russia bilateral treaty on nuclear weapons expired in February, Trump called for a “better agreement” including China. Beijing at the time declined to join disarmament negotiations. But in a call this week, China’s top diplomat Wang Yi and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio “agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearisation”, the US State Department said. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi meets with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, July 11, 2025. Photo: Ministry of Foreign Affairs. “We’re going to talk about denuclearisation — tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes, right?” Trump told reporters on Monday. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said that if the three leaders “really commit themselves to a meaningful denuclearisation, it will be a great achievement for the world”. “We have been for a long time… talking and requesting the need of disarmament in the nuclear field, and we believe that we will only be entirely safe when we would be entirely (without) nuclear weapons,” Guterres said during an ASEAN summit in the Philippines. Iran Trump has said the three leaders will also likely discuss his war in Iran. “We’re going to be talking about denuclearization. We’ll talk about Iran. We have Iran in very good shape, but we’ll talk about Iran a little bit,” Trump told reporters on Monday. China, a top economic partner of Iran, has long sought to mediate in the conflict triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Tehran. The months-long crisis has disrupted global shipping and sent oil prices soaring globally. Trump said in late October that the United States had knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets. China, meanwhile, said avoiding a return to hostilities is a “top priority”, and has in recent weeks hosted leaders and diplomats from various Middle Eastern countries in an effort to persuade parties back to the negotiating table. ‘European conflict’ In contrast, the subject of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine could prove to be a no-go during the talks this week. A Wall Street Journal report last month said that Putin wanted the three-way talks to broker a peace deal in Ukraine that would be favourable to Moscow, which launched its invasion in 2022. It is unlikely, though, that Xi would touch on the highly sensitive topic. US President Donald Trump (right) and President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky (left). File photo: The White House, via Flickr. American officials had said Trump was not expected to raise the issue, but the US president said Monday the leaders would address Ukraine. “We’ll talk about my favourite subject, Ukraine,” Trump told reporters, noting the casualties on both sides of the conflict. Still, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has said Xi showed “irritation” in a recent meeting when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up. “He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Steinmeier told ARD. That has done little to assuage Kyiv, which is anxious about being sidelined on the issue. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has warned that the meeting could be a Yalta-like “redistribution of spheres of influence” for the 21st century. See also: Xi-Trump-Putin summit in Shenzhen evokes 1945 Yalta carve-up The Yalta summit of 1945 saw US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin carve up new post-WWII territorial boundaries with little concern for other countries. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said a meeting between US, Chinese and Russian leaders would “only encourage Putin to continue this war”.

title: Russian Tu-95 Bombers Arrive In Vietnam After Flurry Of Northeast Asia Air Alerts
zh_title: 东北亚空中警报频发后，俄罗斯Tu-95轰炸机抵达越南
summary: 俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，Tu-95MS 飞行员于 2026 年 1 月 21 日在日本海上空进行了一次飞行。照片由 Russian Defence Min 摄
content:
俄罗斯派遣两架Tu-95MS“熊”轰炸机罕见地访问越南。不同寻常的是，这架飞机似乎短暂侵入日本领空，并沿途穿过台湾防空识别区（ADIZ）。此次活动距离中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将在中国深圳举行史无前例的三边会议仅48小时。一段视频的屏幕截图显示，2026 年 1 月 21 日，一架 Tu-95MS 的飞行员在前一次飞越日本海时。照片由俄罗斯国防部/阿纳多卢通过 Getty Images 拍摄 Anadolu 11 月 16 日至 17 日，Tu-95MS 轰炸机是几架俄罗斯军用飞机之一，在东北亚进行了广泛的演习，引发了三个地区政府的防空反应。据分析师 AviVector 称，共有五架涡轮螺旋桨动力轰炸机于 11 月 16 日从俄罗斯远东的乌克兰基地起飞。据报道，其中三架轰炸机在三架 Il-78M Midas 空中加油机的支援下，在日本海上空进行了大约 11 小时的训练飞行。据报道，一架 A-50U Mainstay 空中预警和控制飞机也在日本海上空飞行。与此同时，另外两架 Tu-95MS 继续向南驶向越南。今天，乌克兰空军基地的三架 Tu-95MS 和三架 Il-78M 在日本海上空进行了 11 小时的训练飞行。
一架 A-50U（RF-94268，红色 41）从符拉迪沃斯托克机场起飞，在日本海上空进行了一次侦察飞行。两架 Tu-95MS（RF-94202，红色 43；RF-94188，红色 44）… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) 11 月 17 日， 2026 日本和台湾均未正式确定参与各自空域事件的飞机类型。日本防卫省证实，11 月 17 日早些时候，两架据信是俄罗斯的飞机侵犯了福冈县冲之岛西北部的领空。第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分左右进入，于凌晨 4 点 10 分起飞。第二架飞机于凌晨 4 点 09 分左右进入，于 2026 年 4 月 10 日起飞。据日本防卫省称，凌晨 4 点 12 分，日本认为俄罗斯飞机于 11 月 17 日早些时候进入福冈附近冲之岛西北部的日本领空，第一架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分左右进入日本领空，第二架飞机于当地时间凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分左右进入日本… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — 台湾安全监察站 (@TaiwanMonitor) 2026 年 11 月 17 日，日本防卫省称，日本航空自卫队 (JASDF) 紧急出动西方防空部队的战斗机，发出警告并采取其他措施。
穿过对马海峡后，飞机在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后继续进入太平洋。 2026年11月17日，推测的俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本联合参谋部 该航线使飞机经过连接日本海、东海和西太平洋的几个具有重要战略意义的海上通道。据报道，俄罗斯飞机随后进入韩国防空识别区（KADIZ）。不过，据韩国国防部称，此次事件并未侵犯韩国领空。

【原文 English Original】
Russia has sent a pair of Tu-95MS Bear bombers for a rare visit to Vietnam. Unusually, the aircraft appear to have briefly intruded into Japanese airspace and passed through Taiwan’s Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ) along the way. The activity unfolded just 48 hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump are due to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China. A screen grab from a video shows the pilot of a Tu-95MS during a previous flight over the Sea of Japan on January 21, 2026. Photo by Russian Defense Ministry/Anadolu via Getty Images Anadolu The Tu-95MS bombers were among several Russian military aircraft conducting extensive maneuvers across Northeast Asia on November 16-17, prompting air defense responses from three regional governments. According to analyst AviVector , a total of five of the turboprop-powered bombers departed their home base of Ukrainka in Russia’s Far East on November 16. Three of the bombers reportedly conducted an approximately 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan, supported by three Il-78M Midas aerial refueling tankers. An A-50U Mainstay airborne early warning and control aircraft was also reported operating over the Sea of Japan. Meanwhile, the other two Tu-95MS continued south towards Vietnam. Today, three Tu-95MS and three Il-78M from Ukrainka Air Base conducted an 11-hour training flight over the Sea of Japan. An A-50U (RF-94268, 41 Red) from Vladivostok Airport conducted a reconnaissance flight over the Sea of Japan. Two Tu-95MS (RF-94202, 43 Red; RF-94188, 44… https://t.co/ezIP4s4mxl pic.twitter.com/9fvc2QZsFC — AviVector (@avivector) November 17, 2026 Neither Japan nor Taiwan officially identified the aircraft types involved in their respective airspace incidents. Japan’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that two separate aircraft believed to be Russian violated its territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, in Fukuoka Prefecture, early on November 17. The first aircraft entered at approximately 4:07 a.m. local time and departed at 4:10 a.m. A second aircraft entered at approximately 4:09 a.m. and departed at 4:12 a.m. Two aircraft Japan believes are Russian entered Japanese territorial airspace northwest of Okinoshima, off Fukuoka, early Nov. 17, per Japan's Ministry of Defense. The first was inside from about 4:07 to 4:10 a.m. local time and the second from about 4:09 to 4:12 a.m. The Japan… https://t.co/Sj7vHUFDMQ pic.twitter.com/wYbdE7GWTH — Taiwan Security Monitor (台灣安全觀測站) (@TaiwanMonitor) November 17, 2026 The Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) scrambled fighters from its Western Air Defense Force to issue warnings and take other measures, according to the country’s Ministry of Defense. Tokyo subsequently lodged what it described as a strong protest with Moscow over the incident. Japan also provided details of the aircraft’s subsequent route. After passing through the Tsushima Strait , the planes flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan before continuing into the Pacific Ocean. Flight path of the presumed Russian aircraft on November 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office The route placed the aircraft through several strategically important maritime approaches connecting the Sea of Japan , East China Sea , and western Pacific. The Russian aircraft then reportedly entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ). However, there was no violation of South Korean airspace, according to the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff. Finally, Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported detecting two Russian military aircraft entering its ADIZ from the northeast. Overall, 2 sorties of Russian military aircraft were detected early this morning. The aircraft entered #Taiwan 's ADIZ from the northeast, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited the ADIZ south of Taitung. The #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded… — 國防部 Ministry of National Defense, ROC(Taiwan) (@MoNDefense) November 17, 2026 The aircraft proceeded through airspace east of Taiwan before exiting south of Taitung. Taiwan’s armed forces monitored the activity and responded accordingly, the Ministry of National Defense said. The incident is notable because Taiwan’s defence ministry publicly identified the aircraft as Russian, rather than simply reporting unidentified military aircraft activity. As we have reported in the past , Chinese aircraft commonly fly into the southwestern part of Taiwan’s ADIZ. It is, however, worth noting that the ADIZ declared by Taiwan covers not only the entirety of the Strait but also portions of mainland China. In terms of Russian aircraft operating in Taiwan’s ADIZ, there are historical precedents, but such activity has been greatly reduced since the end of the Cold War. Taiwanese military analyst Chieh Chung told Focus Taiwan that Soviet and Russian military aircraft had previously operated inside Taiwan’s ADIZ in 1986 and January 2010. "The incident was not the first time Russian or former Soviet military aircraft had entered Taiwan's ADIZ, although such flights have become much less frequent since the end of the Cold War." https://t.co/TPUJL9hfp1 https://t.co/SDB6p3E3pD — Bryce C. Barros 白若詩 (@barros_bryce) November 17, 2026 The two remaining Tu-95MS aircraft continued south towards Vietnam and were subsequently reported at Da Nang on November 17. They were accompanied by a pair of Il-76MD Candid transports, one of which was a modernized -90A variant , to support the deployment. Tu-95MS strategic missile carriers RF-94202, RF-94188. Il-76MD, Da Nang Airport / "Danang 35K Feet". pic.twitter.com/22DaoD8PLP — Massimo Frantarelli (@MrFrantarelli) November 17, 2026 [Russie Vietnam] 2 Tu-95MS des forces aérospatiales russes sont arrivés à l'aéroport international de Da Nang (DAD/VVDN), au Vietnam. 2 avions de transport militaire IL-76 (MD et MD-90A) les accompagnaient. (c) AviaNews pic.twitter.com/4bWfFXFOik — La souris (@La_souris_DA) November 17, 2026 The flights took place against the backdrop of preparations for the November 19 meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin in China. The summit is set to be held on the sidelines of meetings of the  Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), which kick off tomorrow. Putin arrived in Shenzhen today. Trump has traveled first to the Philippines as part of a short tour of Asia before heading to China. Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen in the early hours of Nov. 18 to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. ： @PDChina pic.twitter.com/5YotpjYY6R — Shenzhen Daily (@szdaily1) November 17, 2026 The proximity of the Russian operation to the Shenzhen meeting raises questions about the strategic signaling of the Russian flights, particularly as the three governments prepare to discuss nuclear arms control, regional security, and other major international issues. The meeting is particularly unusual given the different priorities each leader is bringing to the table . Trump has indicated that he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and addressing the war in Iran. The expiration of the New START treaty in February 2026 removed the remaining bilateral limits on U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear forces, adding urgency to the question of future arms-control arrangements. U.S. President Barack Obama, at left, and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, at right, shake hands after signing the New START treaty in 2010. Government of Russia Washington has tempered expectations of an immediate agreement, describing the gathering as an initial opportunity for the three nuclear powers to begin a conversation. Putin, meanwhile, is expected to seek discussion of Russia’s war against Ukraine and the possibility of a negotiated settlement. Moscow has signalled that Ukraine will remain a priority in its discussions with Washington. Beijing’s position is more cautious. China has resisted joining trilateral nuclear arms-control negotiations at this stage, arguing that its nuclear arsenal remains substantially smaller than those of the United States and Russia. Xi is also seeking to present China as a central diplomatic actor capable of facilitating dialogue between the other two powers. An apparent new field of Chinese intercontinental ballistic missile silos identified by Matt Korda and Hans Kristensen from the Federation of American Scientists (FAS) and located near the city of Hami in the eastern end of Xinjiang province, in the northwest of China. Kristensen/Korda/FAS 2021 The timing of the Russian aviation activity is therefore difficult to ignore. The operation demonstrated the geographic reach of Russian long-range aviation, with aircraft moving from Russia’s Far East through the approaches to Japan and Taiwan before continuing towards Vietnam. The Southeast Asian nation was a regular late Cold War operating location for Soviet naval Tu-95 Bear reconnaissance aircraft. Of course, as well as strategic signalling, flights of this kind provide valuable long-range training and intelligence collection, including assessment of regional air defense responses. The November 19 meeting may not produce an agreement on nuclear weapons or other major disputes. Still, the Russian flights underscore the fact that strategic stability in the Indo-Pacific also involves the security concerns of the regional states operating along the approaches to the western Pacific. content:
2026 年 11 月 12 日可疑俄罗斯飞机的飞行路线。 日本防卫大臣周二宣布，可疑俄罗斯飞机周四两次侵犯日本领空，促使战斗机紧急升空予以回应。日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周二的例行新闻发布会上表示，周四凌晨 4 点 07 分至 4 点 10 分，一架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯了东海冲之岛西北部的日本领空。随后，凌晨 4 点 09 分至 4 点 12 分，第二架疑似俄罗斯飞机侵犯同一地区的日本领空。飞机穿过对马海峡，在与那国岛和台湾之间飞行，然后进入菲律宾海。作为回应，日本航空自卫队西部防空司令部的日本航空自卫队战斗机紧急紧急升空。日本飞机向可疑的俄罗斯飞机发出了通知和警告。日本飞机无法看到俄罗斯飞机，也无法目视确认进入该空域的飞机类型。
会议记录显示，小泉纯一郎表示：“虽然很难明确说明俄罗斯飞机这次行动背后的意图或目的，但无论如何，防卫省和自卫队将继续高度关注俄罗斯的军事行动，并将采取一切可能措施，确保对领空侵犯保持警惕、监视和适当反应。”不仅侵犯了日本的主权，而且对日本的安全构成了威胁。小泉表示，日本政府已通过外交渠道向俄罗斯政府提出抗议，要求类似事件不再重演。俄罗斯飞机周四进入日本、韩国和台湾的防空识别区（ADIZ）。防空识别区始于主权空域结束处，是一段确定的国际空域，为了国家安全利益，在其中检测和跟踪飞机。战斗机经常紧急起飞拦截和跟踪外国飞机，直到其离开防空识别区。虽然国际法不承认，但许多国家都设有防空识别区，因为领空距离一个国家的海岸线仅延伸 12 海里。这三个国家没有确认这架俄罗斯飞机的身份。
据当地航空观察员称，当天晚些时候，两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 IL-76 运输机降落在越南岘港国际机场。岘港的一个社区社交媒体页面发布了轰炸机抵达的照片以及停在机场的四架俄罗斯飞机的视频。截至发稿时，俄罗斯和越南均已就越南境内出现轰炸机问题发表官方声明。日本军队于 2026 年 6 月 27 日拍摄到一架俄罗斯 Tu-95 轰炸机。日本联合参谋部照片 2015年，路透社报道称，美国已要求越南停止允许俄罗斯加油机使用金兰湾。据报道，这些加油机被用来为在关岛附近进行挑衅性飞行的俄罗斯轰炸机加油。俄罗斯轰炸机最后一次部署到东南亚是在 2017 年 12 月 5 日，当时两架 Tu-95MS 轰炸机和两架 Il-76 运输机降落在印度尼西亚比亚克岛。印尼空军表示，此次访问的目的是

【原文 English Original】
Flight path of the suspect Russian aircraft on Nov. 12, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office map Suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese territorial airspace twice on Thursdays, prompting fighter aircraft to be scrambled in response, Japan’s Defense Minister announced Tuesday. Between 4:07 and 4:10 a.m. on Thursday, one suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace northwest of Okinoshima, which lies in the East China Sea, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said in his regularly scheduled Tuesday press conference. Subsequently, between 4:09 and 4:12 a.m., a second suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace in the same area. The aircraft passed through the Tsushima Strait, flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan, and proceeded into the Philippine Sea. Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft from the JASDF’s Western Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. The Japanese aircraft issued notifications and warnings to the suspected Russian aircraft. Japan’s aircraft were unable to see the Russian aircraft and visually confirm the type of aircraft that entered the airspace. “Whilst it is difficult to state with certainty the intent or purpose behind the Russian aircraft’s actions on this occasion, the Ministry of Defense and the Self-Defense Forces will, in any case, continue to monitor Russia’s military movements with the utmost attention and will take every possible measure to ensure vigilance, surveillance and appropriate responses to airspace violations,” said Koizumi, according to a transcript of the conference . Koizumi called the violation of Japan’s territorial airspace by Russian aircraft not only a serious infringement of Japan’s sovereignty but also a threat to Japan’s security. The Japanese government has lodged a protest with the Russian government through diplomatic channels and demanded that such incidents not be repeated, Koizumi said. The Russian aircraft entered the Air Defense Identification Zones (ADIZs) of Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Thursday. An ADIZ begins where sovereign airspace ends and is a defined stretch of international airspace in which aircraft are detected and tracked in the interest of national security. Fighter aircraft are often scrambled to intercept and shadow the foreign aircraft until it leaves the ADIZ. While not recognized under international law, a number of countries have ADIZs because territorial airspace extends just 12 nautical miles from a country’s coastline. The three countries did not identify the Russian aircraft. Two Tu-95MS bombers and two IL-76 transports landed at Da Nang International Airport, Vietnam, later that day, according to local aviation spotters. A Da Nang-based community social media page posted photos of the bombers arriving and videos of the four Russian aircraft parked at the airport. Russia nor Vietnam, as of publication, have issued official statements on the presence of the bombers in Vietnam. A Russian Tu-95 bomber photographed June 27, 2026, by Japanese forces. Japan Joint Staff Office photo In 2015, Reuters reported that the U.S. had requested Vietnam to stop allowing Russian tanker aircraft to use Cam Ranh Bay. The tankers were reportedly being used to refuel Russian bombers that conducted provocative flights near Guam. The last known Russian bomber deployment to Southeast Asia was on Dec. 5, 2017, when two Tu-95MS bombers and two Il-76 transports landed on Biak Island, Indonesia. The Indonesian Air Force said that the visit was for a navigation exercise. The Russian Defense Ministry said at the time that the bombers were refuelled in the air by Ilyushin Il-78 tankers over the Pacific Ocean. The last time a Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace was on Sept. 23, 2024 , when a Russian IL-38 Maritime Patrol Aircraft violated Japan’s territorial airspace three times north of Rebun Island. The Defense Minister Minoru Kihara said at the time that JASDF F-15J and F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft were scrambled and discharged flares after the Russian aircraft appeared to have ignored the warnings issued. The incident was the first time Japan had released flares against foreign aircraft.

title: Jensen Huang and the Myth of Indispensability
zh_title: 黄仁勋与不可或缺的神话
summary: 这是《大西洋日报》的一个版本，是一份时事通讯，可引导您了解当天最大的故事，帮助您发现新想法，并推荐最好的文化。在这里注册。黄仁勋在今天早上的一份声明中表示，他将“很荣幸”重返计算机芯片巨头英伟达，他上周刚刚被该公司赶下台。对于黄来说不幸的是，该公司董事会在今天的财报电话会议上明确表示，不考虑重新雇用他。但硅谷的主要人物一直在表现出他们的持续支持。对于另一个不太强大的执行官
content:
这是《大西洋日报》的一个版本，是一份时事通讯，可引导您了解当天最大的故事，帮助您发现新想法，并推荐最好的文化。在这里注册。黄仁勋在今天早上的一份声明中表示，他将“很荣幸”重返计算机芯片巨头英伟达，他上周刚刚被该公司赶下台。对于黄来说不幸的是，该公司董事会在今天的财报电话会议上明确表示，不考虑重新雇用他。但硅谷的主要人物一直在表现出他们的持续支持。对于另一位权力较小的高管来说，有关与三名女性发生婚外情的报道（其中一名据称是中国间谍，另一名是直接下属）可能会被视为不可挽回的判断失误。然而，黄的代言人似乎并不认为这就是他在公司职业生涯的结束。 “如果没有詹森，”埃隆·马斯克本周末在 X 上声称，英伟达将失去黄仁勋亲自谈判的重要“握手”交易。加文·贝克（Gavin Baker）的公司投资了英伟达，他写道，随着调查的结束，他支持恢复黄的职位。
Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 在 X 上表示，“动机粗略的记者”有效地“煽动”了董事会，推出了“一代人一次的梦想家”。 Uber 联合创始人特拉维斯·卡兰尼克 (Travis Kalanick) 对科技公司的罢免略知一二，他是请愿书上签名者之一，请愿书要求黄仁勋恢复公司首席执行官职务，马斯克、贝克和斯威尼也是如此。 据《华尔街日报》报道，英伟达的一名高级员工致信该公司董事会，警告称，如果黄仁勋不恢复职务，“不可替代的人才”可能会离开。昨天，当特朗普总统被问及是否支持亲密盟友黄仁勋回归时，他告诉记者，“我不介意”。最终，这些人都无法完全掌控黄的命运。该权力属于英伟达董事会。尽管黄的行为明显违反了资格，但对他的支持证明了这个人对英伟达和整个经济的影响力。 （另一位科技巨头萨姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）的戏剧性解雇和重新聘用也可能说明了这一点。）尽管黄被指控危害国家安全，而且据报道美国证券交易委员会正在调查英伟达是否违反了投资者信息披露法，但他的支持者坚称他仍然是不可或缺的。他们的论点是，他就是公司，失去他的风险实际上可能超过让他重新担任首席执行官的风险。
在某种程度上，他们是对的：黄仁勋已经使自己成为了英伟达的代名词。但他的中心地位是一种负担，而不是一种资产。现在应该反思过度依赖任何一位首席执行官的风险，但业内许多人却强化了相反的教训，加倍押注于一位名誉扫地的高管。英伟达可能被称为“具有系统重要性”的机构——这是一家行业术语，指的是一家其失败将破坏部分金融体系稳定的公司。有关黄仁勋的爆料导致英伟达股票抛售约 1.5 万亿美元（相当于该公司价值的 25% 以上），华尔街为之颤抖。人工智能行业，乃至整个美国经济，都严重依赖该公司的芯片。 “英伟达的大部分金融系统都处于人质状态，”我的同事查理·沃泽尔上周写道。 “黄的规模太大了，不能倒。”

【原文 English Original】
This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. Jensen Huang said in a statement this morning that he would be “honored” to return to Nvidia, the computer-chip giant from which he was ousted just last week. Unfortunately for Huang, the company’s board made it clear on today’s earnings call that it’s not considering rehiring him. But major figures in Silicon Valley have been making a show of their continued support. For another, less powerful executive, reports of extramarital affairs with three women —one of whom is alleged to be a Chinese spy and another of whom was a direct subordinate—would likely be seen as irredeemable lapses in judgment. Yet Huang’s endorsers don’t seem to view this as the end of his career at the company. “Without Jensen,” Elon Musk claimed on X this weekend, Nvidia will lose important “handshake” deals that Huang personally negotiated. Gavin Baker, whose firm invests in Nvidia, has written that he’s in favor of reinstating Huang as the investigations play out. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney remarked on X that “journalists with sketchy motives” effectively “gaslit” the board into pushing out a “once-in-generation visionary.” An Uber co-founder, Travis Kalanick, who knows a thing or two about tech ousters , was among the more than 195,000 signatories of a petition to reinstate Huang as the company’s CEO—as were Musk, Baker, and Sweeney. The Wall Street Journal reports that a high-level Nvidia employee sent a letter to the company’s board warning that “irreplaceable talent” might leave if Huang isn’t reinstated. When President Trump was asked yesterday whether he’d support the return of Huang, a close ally, he told reporters, “I would not mind that.” Ultimately, none of these people has full control over Huang’s fate. That power belongs to Nvidia’s board of directors. But the support for Huang, despite his clearly disqualifying transgressions, is a testament to the power that this one man has held over Nvidia and the economy at large. (It may also be informed by the dramatic firing and rehiring of another tech titan: Sam Altman.) Even though Huang is accused of having jeopardized national security, and the Securities and Exchange Commission is now reportedly probing whether Nvidia violated investor-disclosure laws, his backers insist that he remains indispensable. Their argument is that he is the company, and that the risks of losing him might actually outweigh the risks of bringing him back as CEO. In a way, they are right: Huang has made himself synonymous with Nvidia. But his centrality is a liability rather than an asset. This moment should be a reckoning about the risks of relying so heavily on any one CEO—yet many in the industry are reinforcing the opposite lesson, doubling down on a disgraced executive. Nvidia is what you might call a “systematically important” institution—industry lingo for a company whose failure would destabilize parts of the financial system. Wall Street trembled after the revelations about Huang spurred a roughly $1.5 trillion sell-off in Nvidia stock (equivalent to more than 25 percent of the company’s value). The AI sector, and in turn the entire U.S. economy, is heavily dependent on the firm’s chips. “Nvidia has much of the financial system in a hostage situation,” my colleague Charlie Warzel wrote last week. “Huang is too big to fail. Which may be why so many people seem motivated to downplay or protect him right now.” Some of this is owed to the myth of the tech leader as an irreplaceable genius—a story that Silicon Valley loves to tell. As The Washington Post points out , nearly a tenth of the value of the S&P 500 is tied to companies with no clear successor: Nvidia, Tesla, and Meta. Huang himself liked to boast about his famously flat org structure—he had 60 direct reports. The New York Times notes that Nvidia’s board, which is now investigating whether Huang was the target of Chinese espionage, has a history of “loyalty and deference” to him. Some of its directors have been on the board since 1993. Public outcry has been an effective tactic in bringing back ousted tech leaders in the past; in late 2023, OpenAI’s board fired Altman because he “was not consistently candid in his communications” with them—but reinstated him five days later after a company-wide revolt. Like Huang, Altman is a celebrity co-founder. He’s the face of his company and the person seen as largely responsible for its success. Any of Altman’s shortcomings or misdeeds were considered secondary to, and distinct from, his ability to generate value for shareholders. Obviously, this isn’t the first case of an executive facing consequences over a relationship with an employee: McDonald’s fired its CEO over this in 2019, Intel’s CEO resigned in 2018 after failing to disclose a relationship with a subordinate, Boeing pushed out its CEO in 2006 over a similar situation. The ongoing national-security concerns add another layer of urgency to the situation. The question of how much Huang actually knew about Megaspeed—the company that the alleged Chinese spy worked for, which the U.S. Department of Commerce has been looking into since 2024—is currently under investigation. Investors are angry enough that they’re suing Nvidia over the fiasco (the company had initially denied that there was anything “unusual or unexpected” about its CEO’s relationship with the Megaspeed executive until Huang himself admitted to it; Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment). Not everyone is pushing for Huang’s comeback. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has suggested that he’d like to see Nvidia pick a new CEO from outside the company, and some lawmakers have opposed the idea of Huang’s return. But those who want him reinstated are selling a dangerous narrative about the indispensability of any one leader. The celebrity investor Balaji Srinivasan wrote today that “it’s arguably a matter of US national security to immediately return the most important person in AI to his role at the top AI company”—never mind that Nvidia, under Huang, may have been responsible for allowing the United States’ biggest economic rival to access top-tier computer chips. Tying an entire enterprise to the success or failure of a single person comes with extreme risks; Huang’s defenders are ignoring them. title: ‘We Simply Cannot Trust This Belligerent Neighbor’
zh_title: “我们根本无法信任这个好战的邻居”
summary: 希望抵制中国地区霸权野心的亚洲国家可能会从最近在韩国举办的艺术节中寻找灵感。光州双年展于 1994 年创办，旨在庆祝亚洲文化和韩国民主。今年 9 月，光州双年展因组织者无视北京声称对台湾拥有主权的决定，决定授予台湾自己的同名展馆而引发争议。但尽管中国外交部要求韩国当局纠正这一“严重违规行为”，双年展组织者却拒绝让步。中国不甘心的代表团拉动
content:
希望抵制中国地区霸权野心的亚洲国家可能会从最近在韩国举办的艺术节中寻找灵感。光州双年展于 1994 年创办，旨在庆祝亚洲文化和韩国民主。今年 9 月，光州双年展因组织者无视北京声称对台湾拥有主权的决定，决定授予台湾自己的同名展馆而引发争议。但尽管中国外交部要求韩国当局纠正这一“严重违规行为”，双年展组织者却拒绝让步。不甘心的中国代表团愤然退出了电影节。这一事件给其他与会者上了宝贵的一课：中国不必总是一意孤行。中国的邻国最好在本周的亚太经合组织峰会上牢记这一点。从表面上看，包括美国在内的太平洋地区国家领导人的年度聚会将展示中国日益增长的实力。作为峰会的东道主，中国国家主席习近平精明地邀请客人来到科技中心深圳，这里是领先的机器人制造商、电信公司华为、顶级无人机制造商和流动机器人出租车的所在地。与此同时，习近平在该地区的主要制衡人物特朗普总统将于明天上任，他的形象将被削弱——在国内不受欢迎，在国外卷入一场代价高昂且有争议的战争，并主持一个刚刚被选民赶出国会的政党。
华盛顿在该地区的传统盟友已经对特朗普在第二任期内出人意料地转向中国感到不安。澳大利亚等国家现在正在努力想办法在没有美国支持保证的情况下保护自己免受中国的侵蚀。 “如果美国不在那里，我们在对抗中国时就会更加谨慎，”西澳大利亚大学珀斯美国亚洲中心首席执行官戈登·弗莱克告诉我。 “但这并不意味着我们不会这样做。”欧洲领导人在大西洋联盟破裂的情况下同样试图捍卫自己的利益以对抗中国，而亚洲国家则不同，他们缺乏一个统一的机构来协调政策或维护集体权力。欧盟可以敦促北京在与欧洲共同市场的贸易问题上做出让步，但太平洋地区各国政府必须自行谈判达成协议。与欧盟成员国相比，这些国家在政治和经济上也更加多样化——有的富裕，有的贫穷；有些是民主国家，有些则不是。这使得传递单一统一消息变得更具挑战性。皮尤研究中心的调查数据显示，马来西亚、新加坡和印度尼西亚超过70%的人对中国有好感，而韩国和印度的这一比例不到30%，日本的这一比例为11%。
[阅读：中国在人工智能战争中的情报政变]然而，在亚洲，对抗中国崛起的赌注比其他任何地方都更高。中国的经济无疑是该地区最具主导地位的——是亚洲第二大经济体日本的四倍多。习近平一直致力于在世界各地投射中国的力量，但他最感兴趣的是统治自己的邻国。正如他在 2014 年一次标志着中国转向更加自信的地区政策的关键演讲中所宣称的那样，“亚洲事务应由亚洲人民来管理，亚洲问题应由亚洲人民解决，亚洲安全应由亚洲人民来维护”。

【原文 English Original】
Asian countries hoping to resist China’s ambitions for regional supremacy might look to a recent art festival in South Korea for inspiration. The Gwangju Biennale, founded in 1994 to celebrate Asian culture and South Korea’s democracy, erupted in controversy in September over the organizers’ decision to grant Taiwan its own self-named pavilion—in defiance of Beijing’s purported claims to the island. But despite the Chinese Foreign Ministry’s demands that the South Korean authorities rectify this “ grave violation ,” the Biennale’s organizers refused to budge. China’s unappeased delegation pulled out of the festival in a huff. The incident offered the other attendees a valuable lesson: China needn’t always get its way. China’s neighbors would do well to keep this in mind during this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. On its surface, the annual gathering of leaders of countries throughout the Pacific region, including the United States, will be a showcase of China’s growing power. As the summit’s host, Chinese President Xi Jinping has savvily invited his guests to the tech hub Shenzhen, home to leading robotics manufacturers, the telecommunications firm Huawei, top drone makers, and roving robotaxis. Meanwhile, President Trump, Xi’s main counterweight in the region, will arrive tomorrow as a diminished figure—unpopular at home, entangled in a costly and controversial war abroad, and presiding over a party that voters just cast out of Congress. Washington’s traditional allies in the region have already been rattled by Trump’s unexpected turn toward China in his second term. Countries such as Australia are now working to figure out how to protect themselves against China’s encroaching power without the assurance of American support. “If the U.S. isn’t there, we are going to be a little bit more circumspect about how we stand up to China,” Gordon Flake, the chief executive of the Perth USAsia Centre at the University of Western Australia, told me. “But it doesn’t mean we won’t do it.” Unlike European leaders, who are similarly trying to defend their interests against China amid a breakdown in the Atlantic alliance, the countries of Asia lack a unifying body to coordinate policy or assert collective power. The European Union can press Beijing for concessions on trade with Europe’s common market, but the Pacific region’s various governments must negotiate deals on their own. Compared with EU members, these countries are also more politically and economically diverse—some are wealthy and some are poor; some are democracies and some are not. This makes delivering a single unified message more challenging. More than 70 percent of people in Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia view China favorably, compared with less than 30 percent in South Korea and India, and 11 percent in Japan, according to survey data from the Pew Research Center. [ Read: China’s intelligence coup in the AI war ] Yet the stakes for countering China’s rise are higher in Asia than anywhere else. China’s economy is far and away the most dominant in the region—more than four times that of Japan, Asia’s second-biggest economy. Xi has worked to project China’s power throughout the world, but he is most interested in ruling over his own neighborhood. As he declared in a pivotal 2014 speech that marked the country’s turn toward a more assertive regional policy, “It is for the people of Asia to run the affairs of Asia, solve the problems of Asia, and uphold the security of Asia,” in clear opposition to foreign interference in the region. “The Chinese people, in their pursuit of the Chinese dream of great national renewal, stand ready to support and help other peoples in Asia to realize their own great dreams.” Most countries in the region would prefer to realize their own dreams without China’s “support.” Despite Trump’s inconsistent approach to maintaining ties with long-standing allies, countries such as Japan, South Korea, and Australia are wary of partnering with Xi’s new imperial order instead. Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, having touted the importance of “a multipolar Asia,” dismissed the Asia-for-Asians idea as unrealistic in 2022: “A narrow Asian chauvinism is actually against the continent’s own interest.” India’s leaders have good reason to resist China’s ambitions, which have involved expanding its economic and military influence into South Asia, testing New Delhi’s resolve along their shared Himalayan border, and supporting Pakistan, India’s bitter rival. Beijing “thinks that India needs to accept subordinate status to China,” Manoj Joshi, a fellow at the Observer Research Foundation in New Delhi, told me. But “India is not willing to accept that in any way it is second to China.” Beijing’s contentious territorial claims have other neighbors on edge as well. Xi’s extensive military drills around Taiwan have raised fears of a devastating regional war. His insistent claim to nearly all of the South China Sea keeps China in almost-constant conflict with the Philippines. In July, the Philippine government accused China’s coast guard of allegedly injuring a Filipino sailor in the South China Sea, lamenting in a statement : “We simply cannot trust this belligerent neighbor.” Last month, the Chinese ambassador in Manila drew sharp criticism for provocatively claiming that China “may easily win” a war against the Philippines—though he denied that he was making a threat. Xi has attempted to soften these political conflicts with promises of economic cooperation, but any hope that China’s rise would lift other countries has faded. The same state-subsidized Chinese exports that have threatened industries in the United States and Europe have undercut various sectors throughout Asia as well. Trade with Southeast Asian countries accounts for nearly a quarter of China’s global trade surplus. Chinese companies are expanding their market share in manufacturing industries that are central to South Korea’s economy, such as shipbuilding, batteries, and petrochemicals. Xi has sought to use China’s growing economic might to coerce neighbors to concede to his political demands. Beijing halted supplies of rare earth elements to Japan in January after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi warned that a Chinese invasion of Taiwan could trigger a military response. (Despite this pressure, Japan has not withdrawn its comment.) Even as Trump has cozied up to Xi over the past year, his administration has tried to reassure Asian allies of its continued support. The U.S. conducted naval drills with the Philippines and Japan in the South China Sea in July. Just before this year’s APEC summit, Trump met with his fellow leaders from Australia, India, and Japan for talks about enhanced cooperation on AI, critical minerals, and maritime security, with new plans for joint military exercises to counter China’s power. But other moves add to traditional U.S. allies’ unease. Trump has delayed approval of a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan, presumably to stay on better terms with Xi. Last year Trump flew all the way to South Korea to meet with Xi on the sidelines of the APEC summit, but skipped the summit itself. In the absence of clear signals from Washington, Asian leaders have tightened ties with one another. In 2017, when Trump withdrew from the Trans-Pacific Partnership, a regional trade pact designed to isolate China, the other 11 members moved forward without the United States. Japan has expanded its relationships in the region, in part by offering aid to strengthen the defense capabilities of other Asian countries. Australia and India have deepened their collaboration through expanded intelligence-sharing and joint military exercises. [ Read: The future of AI is not China ] But leaders in the region must tread carefully. They all have close trade links to China and can’t risk alienating their vindictive neighbor. Akio Takahara, an expert on diplomacy at Tokyo Woman’s Christian University, told me that Chinese leaders actively “try to disturb any attempt by other countries to link up.” Ironically, the more powerful China becomes, the more necessary the U.S. is as a counterweight. Flake told me that although there is “acute concern about the reliability of the United States,” policy makers in Australia still view this alliance as crucial to the country’s security—and “there is no clear Plan B.” Instead, they are “striving to get the United States back to where the United States has been.” The fact that the U.S. is still indispensable in Asia indicates the extent of Xi’s failure to dominate the region. Trump’s unpredictable foreign policy has delivered Xi a chance to expand Chinese influence at America’s expense, but the Chinese leader’s heavy-handed pursuit of power has ultimately left the door open for a U.S. revival in his own backyard. Instead of treating his neighbors like imperial subjects, Xi might consider letting Chinese artists participate in the Gwangju Biennale next time and enjoy the party.

title: How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA
zh_title: 中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜
summary: 中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜 H.Seidl 星期二，11/17/2026 - 11:58 图片联盟/新华社 |高泽明评论 2026 年 11 月 17 日 阅读 4 分钟 中国军队的战斗准备如何？解放军的困惑 中国的武装部队比以往任何时候都更有能力，但也陷入混乱。安德鲁·斯科贝尔表示，无论他们有什么缺点，他们在任何战争中都可能成为可怕的对手。 10月下旬中共二十届五中全会选举张胜密将军为中央军事委员会副主席
content:
中国军队的作战准备情况如何？解放军之谜 H.Seidl 星期二，11/17/2026 - 11:58 图片联盟/新华社 |高泽明评论 2026 年 11 月 17 日 阅读 4 分钟 中国军队的战斗准备如何？解放军的困惑 中国的武装部队比以往任何时候都更有能力，但也陷入混乱。安德鲁·斯科贝尔表示，无论他们有什么缺点，他们在任何战争中都可能成为可怕的对手。 10月下旬，中共二十届五中全会选举中央军委副主席张生民将军为中共政治局委员。党的领导层还确认了九月份中央军委高级将领被开除的消息，但没有任命任何继任者。这使得中国相当于美国军队参谋长联席会议的成员从通常的七人减少到只有两名成员：习近平担任文职主席，还有一名穿制服的军官张将军。中国人民解放军（PLA）被许多人认为是中华人民共和国（PRC）历史上最现代化、最有能力、最专业、装备最精良的军队。但它也正在经历自 20 世纪 60 年代毛泽东文化大革命以来的 6 年来最大的动荡。作为习近平反腐运动的一部分，自 2022 年以来，清洗行动已清除了 100 多名高级官员。
值得注意的是，这些被罢黜的将领中，有 50% 到 80% 是各级作战指挥官。 清洗运动震撼了国防机构 与此同时，中国的国防机构仍在承受四十年来最彻底的组织重组的冲击。 2016年启动的这次改革，不仅是为了增强解放军发动二十一世纪联合作战的能力，也是为了精简和集中军队，使其受中央军委主席习近平的直接指挥。这次重组被称为“中国的戈德华特-尼科尔斯”，以强调与美军在越战后时期强制各军种联合作战的举措的相似之处，这一举措花了几十年才完全实施。没有人知道习近平雄心勃勃的计划进展如何，因为中国人民解放军——包括空军、海军、陆军、火箭军和其他特种军种——尚未在21世纪发动战争，战争是对任何一支军队的严峻考验。现代化已将一支技术含量低、以轻步兵为中心、拥有陈旧空军和小型褐水海军的军队转变为一支机械化地面部队​​，拥有大量第四代和第五代战斗机空中力量，以及世界上最大的蓝水海军舰队。
此外，今天的解放军部队进行了更加真实的战斗训练，并且在过去二十年中参加了无数次（尽管大部分是小规模的）多国野战演习。中国武装部队在中国周边地区变得越来越积极主动和具有侵略性。在遥远的西部，地面部队的部署数量越来越多，在两国有争议的喜马拉雅边境沿线与印度军队偶尔发生小规模流血冲突。在南海，中国人民解放军海军、中国海警和海上民兵加大了对海军舰艇、海警快艇和渔船的骚扰力度，特别是菲律宾和越南的海军舰艇、海警快艇和渔船。中国海上力量在东海进行了多次军事演习

【原文 English Original】
How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA H.Seidl Tue, 11/17/2026 - 11:58 picture alliance / Xinhua News Agency | Gao Zeming Comment Nov 17, 2026 4 min read How combat ready is China’s military? The puzzle of the PLA The country’s armed forces are more capable than ever but in turmoil. Whatever their shortcomings, Andrew Scobell says they are likely to prove a formidable adversary in any war. The Fifth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) in late October elected the vice chair of the Central Military Commission (CMC), General Zhang Shengmin, to the CCP Politburo . The party leadership also confirmed the September expulsions of top generals from the CMC, but did not appoint any replacements. This left China’s rough equivalent to the US military’s Joint Chiefs of Staff with just two members, down from its usual seven: Xi Jinping as its civilian chair and one single uniformed officer, General Zhang.   The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is by many accounts the most modern, capable, professional and best equipped military in the history of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). But it is also enduring its greatest upheavals in six decades—since the turmoil of Mao Zedong’s Cultural Revolution in the 1960s. Purges have swept away more than 100 senior officers since 2022 as part of Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption crusade. Remarkably, between 50 and 80 percent of these ousted general officers have been operational commanders at various levels . Purges have rocked the defense establishment At the same time, China’s defense establishment is still absorbing the shock of the most thoroughgoing organizational restructuring in four decades. This revamping, launched in 2016, was not only intended to make the PLA more capable of waging twenty-first century joint warfare, but also to streamline and centralize it under the direct chain of command of CMC chairman Xi. This reorganization, dubbed “ China’s Goldwater-Nichols ” to underscore the parallels with the US military’s post-Vietnam War era initiative to compel separately stovepiped services to fight jointly—an effort that took decades to fully implement.  No one knows how well Xi’s ambitious initiative is faring, since the PLA – comprising the PLA Air Force, PLA Navy, PLA Ground Force, PLA Rocket Force, and other specialized services – has yet to wage war in the 21st century, warfighting being the acid test of any military. Modernization has transformed a low-tech, light infantry-centric military with an antiquated air force and a small brown-water navy into a mechanized ground force, with a sizeable airpower inventory of fourth-  and fifth-generation fighter jets, and the world’s largest blue-water naval fleet. Moreover, today’s PLA units engage in more realistic combat training and, for the past two decades, have participated in numerous, albeit largely small-scale, multinational field exercises. China’s armed forces have become increasingly activist and aggressive around the PRC’s periphery. In the far west, ground forces have deployed in ever greater numbers, engaging in occasional bloody small-scale clashes with India’s army along the two countries’ disputed Himalayan border . In the South China Sea , the PLA Navy, PRC Coast Guard and People’s Maritime Militia have stepped up harassment of naval ships, coast guard cutters and fishing boats, notably those of the Philippines and Vietnam. In the East China Sea , PRC maritime forces have conducted similar operations against Japanese and South Korean vessels. Perhaps most alarming is the dramatic escalation of so-called gray zone provocations around Taiwan. Modernization has strengthened the PLA  PLA formations are also operating further and further from China’s borders. Ground force units have served on United Nations peacekeeping missions around the world, while some air formations have also operated overseas. In 2026, the PLA acknowledged its first air installation outside of the PRC in Laos. Yet the most routinely deployed service overseas has been the PLA Navy. Its vessels have operated continuously in the Gulf of Aden since late 2008 and have been more active across the Western Pacific, Indian Ocean and Mediterranean, and even making appearances in the Atlantic, Arctic and Baltic seas. The PLA Navy has operated a support base in Djibouti on the Red Sea since 2017 and opened a naval base in Ream, Cambodia, in 2025.  But increased peacetime operational experience and tempo do not guarantee wartime successes. While PLA drills and deployments do not seem to have been impacted by the unprecedented waves of purges continuing across all echelons of China’s military, their effects could be different under actual combat conditions. The PLA has not fought a major war since China’s conflict with Vietnam in 1979. Muscular and intimidating shows of force around the PRC’s periphery and the periodic spectacle of smartly turned-out troops with gleaming military hardware on parade in Beijing are not incontrovertible proof of combat readiness. Nevertheless, as a former US defense chief famously remarked , “You go to war with the army you have.” In the event of conflict, the leaders of the PRC – just as much as those of other great powers – will have no choice but to send their militaries into battle irrespective of their condition or level of combat readiness – and their armed forces will salute and follow orders, executing operations as best they can. The PLA will remain something of a puzzle for a while, but it is likely to make a credible account of itself in any conflict. Its combat record over the decades has shown that it can fight effectively, absorb heavy casualties and adapt under fire. The views expressed in this piece are those of the author. title: Kazakhstan Expands Its Role in Eurasian Connectivity Through the Middle Corridor
zh_title: 哈萨克斯坦通过中间走廊扩大其在欧亚互联互通中的作用
