Quad Leaders’ Summit Joint Press Release Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research On November 17, 2026, — President Donald J. Trump of the United States, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese of Australia, Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India, and Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae of Japan — met for a Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila. This year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the tenth anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Prime Minister Abe Shinzo of Japan in 2016. A decade on, that vision is stronger than ever. Together, we have shown that the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability, and prosperity. We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability. We express grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions. We are securing critical supply chains, protecting freedom of navigation and overflight, driving growth through technologies of the future including investments in and deployment of trusted Super Intelligence (SI)*, and responding to disasters with life-saving assistance. We commit to work together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific. We are working with regional partners to tackle shared challenges and drive opportunities to deliver tangible benefits to the Indo-Pacific. We announce the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum which is scheduled to be held in early 2027, bringing together business leaders, government officials, and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater business ties across our private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific. We affirm the importance of the Super Intelligence* Accelerator , announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta. The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted Super Intelligence (SI)* access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific. We are proud to welcome the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration , a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness. In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer. We are proud of progress under the Quad Partnership for Cable Connectivity and Resilience , which has expanded access to secure and trusted communications infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific. Today, we welcome an expansion of Australia’s contribution to the Partnership to focus on electricity cables, strengthening regional energy security and connectivity. We also welcome upcoming undersea cables projects in the Indian Ocean which are intended to strengthen regional connectivity. We acknowledge the rapid increase in the number and scale of cyber incidents in the region and announce enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation , through which we plan to work together to achieve an open and secure cyberspace. We unequivocally condemn terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and commit to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism. We reaffirm our unwavering support for ASEAN centrality and unity.  Together, we are committed to upholding a free and open Indo-Pacific. * In Australia, India, and Japan, ‘Super Intelligence’ refers to ‘artificial intelligence.’ The post Quad Leaders’ Summit Joint Press Release appeared first on The White House .

title: Finland’s Iceye bids €2 billion for Italian rocket maker Avio
zh_title: 芬兰 Iceye 出价 20 亿欧元收购意大利火箭制造商 Avio
summary: 罗马——芬兰运营商 Iceye 向意大利火箭制造商 Avio 提出了 20 亿欧元现金报价（合 22 亿美元），该报价将整合欧洲的太空能力，并让 Iceye 负责 Avio 向美国导弹业务的扩张。拟议的交易符合减少对外部供应商的依赖并缩小与美国和中国行业领导者之间日益扩大的差距的努力。 “欧洲对主权太空和国防能力的需求正在增长。满足这一需求的工业能力建设需要数年时间，这使得现在投资至关重要，”Iceye 周二表示。菲
content:
罗马——芬兰运营商 Iceye 向意大利火箭制造商 Avio 提出了 20 亿欧元现金报价（合 22 亿美元），该报价将整合欧洲的太空能力，并让 Iceye 负责 Avio 向美国导弹业务的扩张。拟议的交易符合减少对外部供应商的依赖并缩小与美国和中国行业领导者之间日益扩大的差距的努力。 “欧洲对主权太空和国防能力的需求正在增长。满足这一需求的工业能力建设需要数年时间，这使得现在投资至关重要，”Iceye 周二表示。该公司表示，将在五年内向意大利 Avio 投资 10 亿欧元，以扩大 Avio Vega 火箭的客户群。芬兰政府支持这一提议，芬兰国防部长安蒂·哈卡宁表示，“如果完成……将创建一个全球航天工业参与者，通过它，芬兰和整个欧洲国防的自给自足的供应安全将上升到一个新的水平。” Avio 周二表示正在考虑这一收购要约，而拥有 Avio 18% 股份的意大利国家控股国防集团 Leonardo 的首席执行官表示，他对这一收购要约感到“惊喜”，并将予以考虑。 Avio 董事会于周二举行了第一次会议，并表示已开始评估此次出价，Iceye 表示，该出价较该意大利集团周一收盘价溢价 21.3%，较其三个月成交量加权平均价溢价 34.8%。
除了欧洲航天发射活动外，Avio 也是导弹固体火箭发动机的市场领导者。9 月，该公司在弗吉尼亚州赫特的美国新设施破土动工，以实现为美国导弹生产带来急需的额外产能的雄心。 Avio 已与雷神公司合作生产 Mk 104 双推力火箭发动机，并与洛克希德·马丁公司合作在 Hurt 为洛克希德的增程 GMLRS (ER GMLRS) 和精确打击导弹 (PrSM) 项目生产发动机。 Avio 发言人告诉《防务新闻》，如果 Iceye 收购，则需要美国政府的批准以及意大利政府的批准。 9月，Avio宣布9个月的订单额为2.37亿欧元，其中一半与国防相关，其余主要与其Vega C和Vega E发射器有关。 Iceye 表示，其每股 41 欧元的报价将通过全资意大利子公司 Iris 2 发起，目的是使该公司退市。消息传出后，Avio 股价上涨超过 15%，至 39.5 欧元左右。 Iceye 自 2022 年以来一直向乌克兰提供卫星雷达图像，上个月与诺基亚和乌克兰国防部签署了一份意向书，探讨太空合作，包括主权卫星通信。
Iceye首席执行官拉法尔·莫德热夫斯基(Rafal Modrzewski)在赫尔辛基的一次活动上发表讲话时表示，该公司在发起竞标之前已与包括政府在内的相关各方进行了磋商，并且还需要几个月的时间才能完成交易。“这是一次非凡的能力组合……遵循相当明确的行业趋势，带来了全面的垂直整合，”莫德热夫斯基表示，并补充说这对两家公司都有利。材料来自路透社，作者 Giulia Segreti 和 Essi Lehto。

【原文 English Original】
ROME — Finnish operator Iceye has a made €2 billion cash offer ($2.2 billion) for Italian rocket maker Avio which would integrate Europe’s space capabilities as well as putting Iceye in charge of Avio’s expansion into the U.S. missile business. The proposed deal fits with efforts to reduce reliance on external providers and narrow a widening gap with industry leaders in the U.S. and China. “Europe’s need for sovereign space and defense capabilities is growing. Building the industrial capacity to meet that demand takes years, which makes it critical to invest now,” said Iceye on Tuesday. The firm said it would invest €1 billion in Avio in Italy over five years in a bid to expand the customer base of Avio’s Vega rocket. The Finnish government backed the offer, with Finnish Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen stating, “If completed … a global space industry player will be created, through which the self-sufficient security of supply of Finland’s and all of Europe’s defense will rise to a new level.” Avio said on Tuesday it was considering the offer, while the CEO of Italian state controlled defense group Leonardo, which owns an 18% percent stake in Avio, said he was “pleasantly surprised” by the bid and would consider it. Avio’s board held a first meeting on Tuesday and said it had started assessing the bid, which Iceye said offered a 21.3% premium to the Italian group’s closing price on Monday or a 34.8% premium to its three-month volume-weighted average price. Apart from its European space launch activity, Avio is also a market leader in solid rocket motors for missiles. In September it broke ground in Hurt, Virginia, on a new U..S facility to fulfill an ambition to bring much needed extra capacity to U.S. missile production. Avio has already partnered with Raytheon on production of the Mk 104 dual-thrust rocket motor and has teamed with Lockheed Martin to produce motors at Hurt for Lockheed’s Extended Range GMLRS (ER GMLRS) and Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) programs. An Avio spokesman told Defense News that U.S. government approval would be required in the event of a takeover by Iceye, as well as Italian government approval. In September, Avio announced a nine month order intake of €237 million, of which half was defense related, with the remainder mainly related to its Vega C and Vega E launchers. Iceye said its €41-per-share offer will be launched through wholly owned Italian subsidiary Iris 2 with the aim of delisting the company. Avio shares climbed more than 15% to around €39.5 on the news. Iceye has supplied Ukraine with satellite radar imagery since 2022, and last month signed a letter of intent with Nokia and Ukraine’s Defence Ministry to explore cooperation in space, including sovereign satellite communications. Speaking at an event in Helsinki, Iceye CEO Rafal Modrzewski said the company had held consultations with the parties involved, including governments, before launching the bid, and that it would take a few more months to close the transaction. “It’s a phenomenal combination of capabilities … bringing a full vertical integration, following quite clear industry trends,” Modrzewski said, adding that it would be beneficial for both companies. With material from Reuters by Giulia Segreti and Essi Lehto.

title: Trump seeks nuclear cuts at summit with Putin and Xi, but prospects are low
zh_title: 特朗普在与普京和习近平的峰会上寻求削减核武器，但前景渺茫
summary: 维也纳——美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人将于周四在中国科技大都市深圳会面，这场会议被各方誉为“历史性”会议。讨论的主题包括削减全球核库存。但专家警告说，虽然会议本身是一个积极的进展，但任何重大突破仍然不太可能。过去一周，人们对这次聚会的期望不断升高，尤其是在俄罗斯，该活动被赋予了“雅尔塔2.0”的色彩，指的是1945年重新安排的会议。
content:
维也纳——美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人将于周四在中国科技大都市深圳会面，这场会议被各方誉为“历史性”会议。讨论的主题包括削减全球核库存。但专家警告说，虽然会议本身是一个积极的进展，但任何重大突破仍然不太可能。过去一周，人们对这次聚会的期望不断升高，尤其是在俄罗斯，这次活动被赋予了“雅尔塔2.0”的色彩，指的是1945年二战后重新安排世界秩序的会议。与此同时，从美国方面来看，特朗普政府在深圳推动有关削减核武器的讨论，令许多观察家感到惊讶。俄罗斯和美国之间的最后一项战略军备控制条约（《新削减战略武器条约》）于 2 月到期，这使得这两个最大的核国家自 1972 年以来首次对原子武库没有数量限制。与此同时，中国不是《新削减战略武器条约》的缔约国，事实上也从未加入过任何类似的战略武器条约。据估计，北京拥有世界第三大核武库，有数百个，尽管分析人士认为，中国近年来一直在努力大幅增加这一数字。美国和俄罗斯各自拥有约 4,000 件核武器库存。
这种数字上的差异也是中国此前对以三边形式讨论战略武器限制的想法感到愤怒的原因，就像美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在会议前夕推动的那样。尽管北京方面已经确认了此次会议，但并未正式表示战略武器对话将提上议程。中国外交部发言人毛宁表示，“三位元首将就维护世界和平、促进大国关系战略稳定深入交换意见。”这避免了明确指出美国的要求。 “总统已明确表示，除其他议题外，他将讨论世界范围内核武器的削减。特朗普总统认为，这种扩散非常危险，”白宫发言人奥利维亚·威尔士上周五告诉记者。总部位于维也纳的开放核网络（一家处理核军备控制问题的国际非政府组织）的研究协调员尼基塔·杰格蒂亚列夫（Nikita Degtyarev）表示，他对可实现的成果持现实态度。 “我没有很高的期望，但我很高兴这一切正在发生，”他在接受采访时说。 “领导人级别的会议不同于正在进行的五常对话和其他现有形式。”五常对话汇集了五个核不扩散条约承认的核武器国家——美国、俄罗斯、中国、法国和英国。
– 在工作层面上讨论核政策和降低风险。“如果三方会议就核问题取得任何成果，那它可能更像是一份政治声明，而不是可核查和限制性的军控协议，”核问题项目主任、华盛顿智库战略与国际研究中心高级研究员希瑟·威廉姆斯说，“我认为最有可能的重大成果将是重申里根-戈尔巴乔夫的口头禅，即核战争不可能获胜，也决不能打。”杰格佳廖夫说道。达成更具实质性或开创性的协议也不太可能，因为根本没有

【原文 English Original】
VIENNA — The leaders of the U.S., Russia and China are set to meet in the Chinese tech metropolis of Shenzhen on Thursday in an event that has been hailed as “historic” by all sides. Among the topics raised for discussion are reductions in global nuclear stockpiles. But experts caution that while the meeting itself is a positive development, any major breakthrough remains unlikely.  Expectations for the get-together ratcheted up over the course of the past week, particularly in Russia, where the event has been ascribed undertones of a “Yalta 2.0,” referencing the 1945 conference that reordered the world after World War II. From the U.S. side, meanwhile, the Trump administration surprised many observers by pushing for discussions about reducing nuclear weapons while in Shenzhen. The last strategic arms control treaty between Russia and the U.S., in the form of New START, expired in February, leaving the two largest nuclear states without numerical limits on atomic arsenals  for the first time since 1972.  China, meanwhile, was not a party to New START and was, in fact, never part of any strategic arms treaty like it. Beijing is estimated to have the third-largest nuclear arsenal in the world, at several hundred, although analysts believe it has been working to significantly increase this number in recent years. The U.S. and Russia each have stockpiles of around 4,000  nuclear weapons.  This numerical discrepancy is also why China has previously bristled at the idea of discussing strategic arms limitation in a trilateral format like the one U.S. President Donald Trump has been pushing in the run-up to the meeting. Although Beijing has confirmed the meeting, it has stopped short of officially saying strategic arms dialogue would be on the agenda. “The three presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations,” said Mao Ning, spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry.  This avoids naming explicitly what the U.S. has asked for. “The President has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” White House spokesperson Olivia Wales told reporters last Friday.  Nikita Degtyarev, research coordinator at the Vienna-based Open Nuclear Network, an international NGO dealing with nuclear arms control, said he was realistic about achievable outcomes. “I don’t have very high expectations, but I’m happy that it’s happening,” he said in an interview. “A meeting at the leader level is something else than the ongoing P5 dialogue and other existing formats.” The P5 dialogue brings together the five Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty-recognized nuclear weapons states – the U.S., Russia, China, France and the U.K. – on a working level to discuss nuclear policy and risk reduction.  “If there is any outcome of the trilateral meeting relating to nuclear issues, it will likely be more of a political statement than a verifiable and restrictive arms control agreement,” said Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Issues and senior fellow at the Washington-based think tank CSIS ,  “I think the most likely significant outcome would be a reiteration of the Reagan-Gorbachev mantra that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought,” Degtyarev said. A more substantive or groundbreaking agreement was also unlikely because there simply wasn’t enough time for lower-level officials to hammer out the details of any possible agreement that the leaders could sign, he said. Major arms control treaties often take years of meticulous crafting at the working level before heads of state come together to sign them.  Trump first raised the topic of denuclearization in the context of the summit to reporters on Oct. 19, a day after the Wall Street Journal first reported about a proposed trilateral meeting.  A possible wildcard agenda item remains in the form of artificial intelligence in nuclear weapons. AI in nuclear command and control has emerged as a somewhat more promising topic and a potential area for agreement more palatable to all sides than commitments to numerical reductions or verification mechanisms. The South China Morning Post reported Nov. 11, citing sources familiar with preparations, that working-level teams had discussed AI in critical weapons systems and that the agenda was shifting toward potential common ground, particularly AI’s role in nuclear command and control. One source characterized AI governance of nuclear weapons as an “easy deliverable” consistent with past policies. This “could give Trump something to announce without requiring anyone to compromise their nuclear posture,” Lizzi Lee, a fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute, told the French press agency AFP .  Under the previous U.S. administration, Biden and Xi reaffirmed the importance of human decision-making in nuclear command and control in November 2024, while Russia has so far resisted such language, including in the P5 process.  Much may depend on the willingness of Beijing to engage in strategic arms dialogue, which has indicated it has no major desire to discuss this topic while China remains a numerical underdog in the quantity of its warheads. “China is the host and will probably closely stage-manage the event and the agenda,” Degtyarev said. Xi Jinping’s style of international engagements tends to be highly scripted and predictable, at odds with Trump’s more improvisational approach.  The common denominator for all three leaders is more likely to be good publicity. “Trump is probably genuine about his interest in nuclear arms reduction,” Degtyarev assessed, “but probably also from a self-serving and PR point of view.”  Though the meeting is historic in nature for its assembling of a triumvirate of the world’s most powerful men, “the Yalta 2.0 comparisons are overblown,” said Degtyarev. “The scale of the historical moment is simply different.”

title: New pact positions the Philippines as a defense hub for Australian troops
zh_title: 新协议将菲律宾定位为澳大利亚军队的防御中心
summary: 菲律宾马尼拉——澳大利亚和菲律宾高级官员签署了一项防务协议，以加速军事协调，为轮换部队部署和澳大利亚对菲律宾军事基础设施的投资铺平道路。 11 月 15 日签署的防务合作协议（DCA）旨在消除行政瓶颈并创建更有效的协调系统，以快速跟踪双边防务活动。到目前为止，两国的军事交流基本上是根据1995年的协议备忘录进行的，而部队交流则以互访地位为指导。
content:
菲律宾马尼拉——澳大利亚和菲律宾高级官员签署了一项防务协议，以加速军事协调，为轮换部队部署和澳大利亚对菲律宾军事基础设施的投资铺平道路。 11 月 15 日签署的防务合作协议（DCA）旨在消除行政瓶颈并创建更有效的协调系统，以快速跟踪双边防务活动。到目前为止，两国的军事交流主要根据1995年的协议备忘录进行，而部队交流则以2007年签署并自2012年起生效的《访问部队地位协议》为指导。据澳大利亚国防部称，新协议涵盖情报共享、军事训练、空中和地面无人机的转让、海上活动和军事基础设施。副总理理查德·马勒斯在一份声明中表示：“这项新的防务合作安排将深化我们国防军之间的务实合作，并为共同支持地区安全创造新的机会。”菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗表示，新的 DCA 减少了官僚主义障碍，特别是在部队部署方面，并使澳大利亚能够迅速部署部队来援助菲律宾的救灾工作。特奥多罗在签约后对记者表示：“做一件事不再是 100 个步骤，而是现在只需要 10 个……而且这将更有目的性，而不是临时性的。”
此举正值澳大利亚重新调整其防御态势，以应对中国在印太地区不断扩大的军事能力、不断扩大的导弹射程以及越来越多地使用灰色地带战术和经济胁迫。菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯（中）和第一夫人路易丝·阿拉内塔-马科斯（右）在 11 月 16 日于马尼拉举行的第 49 届东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 峰会期间的晚宴前欢迎澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯 (Anthony Albanese)。 2026 年。（Nhac Nguyen / POOL / 法新社，盖蒂图片社）“从澳大利亚的角度来看，菲律宾是我们的第一道防线，”澳大利亚战略政策研究所高级研究员尤安·格雷厄姆告诉《防务新闻》。澳大利亚遭受了解放军部队的骚扰，包括危险的海上演习、在其北部专属经济区进行激光瞄准，以及在澳大利亚皇家海军舰艇附近使用声纳和照明弹。与澳大利亚一样，菲律宾也面临着中国的压力。中国船只使用高能水炮、军用级激光，撞击和攻击菲律宾武装部队船只和人员。当被问及 DCA 是否旨在增强台湾海峡的威慑力时，特奥多罗强调该协议将增强“西菲律宾海”和“菲律宾领土”的威慑力。战略转变 澳大利亚标志着和平时期向 2023 年否认战略的历史性转变，最近将其写入 2026 年国防战略。
这个想法是将澳大利亚国防军重塑为一支一体化、集中的军队，能够威慑和阻止其进入其北部通道，其中包括部署前沿防御部队。今年早些时候，澳大利亚在总部位于布里斯班的第18保障旅下成立了新的濒海机动大队，以向更北的地区作战，使菲律宾成为该战略的重要组成部分。但分析师格雷厄姆警告称，澳大利亚只能部署小型部队。并保留这些莫

【原文 English Original】
MANILA, Philippines — Top officials from Australia and the Philippines have inked a defense pact to accelerate military coordination, paving the way for rotational troop deployment and Australian investments in Philippine military infrastructure. The Nov. 15 Defense Cooperation Agreement, or DCA, is designed to cut administrative bottlenecks and create a more efficient coordination system to fast-track bilateral defense activities. So far the two countries’ military exchanges have largely fallen under a 1995 memorandum of agreement, while troop exchanges were guided by the Status of Visiting Forces Agreement, signed in 2007 and effective since 2012. According to Australia’s Department of Defence, the new pact covers intelligence-sharing, military training, the transfer of aerial and surface drones, maritime activities, and military infrastructure. “This new Defence Cooperation Arrangement will deepen practical cooperation between our defense forces and create new opportunities to work together in support of regional security,” Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles said in a statement. Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said the new DCA reduces bureaucratic barriers, particularly in troop deployment, and would allow Australia to rapidly deploy troops to aid in Philippine disaster response. “Rather than 100 steps to do a single thing, it will just now take 10 … and it will be more purposeful and not ad hoc,” Teodoro told reporters following the signing. The move comes as Australia recalibrates its defense posture in response to China’s expanding military capabilities, growing missile reach, and increasing use of gray-zone tactics and economic coercion in the Indo-Pacific. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. (C) and First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos (R) welcome Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ahead of the Gala Dinner during the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on Nov. 16, 2026. (Nhac Nguyen / POOL / AFP via Getty Images) “From Australia’s point of view, the Philippines is our first line of defense,” Australian Strategic Policy Institute senior fellow Euan Graham told Defense News. Australia has experienced harassment by PLA forces, including dangerous maritime maneuvers, laser targeting in its northern exclusive economic zone, and the use of sonar and flares in close proximity to Royal Australian Navy vessels. Like Australia, the Philippines faces Chinese pressure head-on. Chinese ships have used high-powered water cannons, pointed military-grade lasers, rammed, and attacked Armed Forces of the Philippines vessels and personnel. When asked if the DCA was meant to boost deterrence in the Taiwan Strait, Teodoro emphasized the agreement will bolster “deterrence in the West Philippine Sea” and in “Philippine territory.” Strategy shift Australia marked a historic peacetime shift toward a strategy of denial in 2023, most recently codified in the 2026 national defense strategy. The idea is to reshape the Australian Defense Force into an integrated, focused military capable of deterring and denying access to its northern approaches, which includes deploying a forward-defense force. Earlier this year, Australia created the new Littoral Maneuver Group under the 18th Sustainment Brigade headquartered in Brisbane, to operate farther north, making the Philippines an important part of that strategy. But Australia can only deploy small units, analyst Graham cautioned. And keeping these mobile forces supplied and operational in archipelagic countries like the Philippines is challenging, as troops and equipment are moved across widely dispersed islands during operations. Building logistics networks To that end, the new cooperation agreement is expected to facilitate discussions on potential Australian investments in Philippine military infrastructure. A list of five Luzon bases slated to receive funding for eight infrastructure projects was expected to be finalized around August this year. However, only one base has been discussed in detail so far, officials told Defense News. Teodoro previously clarified that base agreements with Australia will follow a different model than the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) between the Philippines and the United States, which includes provisions for prepositioning military equipment and assets. The Australian “basing” arrangements, officials said, would include areas that are not traditional bases. Rather than a large basing presence, what the Australian military needs is access to locations that could sustain its forces during operations and contingencies. Discussions so far have included sustainment and logistics to support joint operations while troops spread across the archipelago’s most complex, most challenging, and remote terrains. Graham said Australia’s role in the Philippines is distinct but complementary to that of the United States. While physical locations could overlap, the infrastructure projects would be different.  Canberra and Manila in 2021 signed the Mutual Support Logistics Arrangement, which covers fuel and other supplies for aircraft and vessels, transportation, logistics, and coordination. “The importance of logistics can’t be underestimated. It’s not just about getting your fighting force fighting. You’ve got to supply them with food, fuel, and ammunition during all of that,” Graham said. More complex training With the new DCA with Australia in place, joint exercises , especially Exercise ALON, will see a larger iteration next year, Teodoro said. Exercise ALON, first held in 2023, is the biennial flagship joint training exercise between countries, focused on amphibious operations. The 2025 edition saw Australia’s largest overseas military exercise for the year and showcased the ADF projecting combat forces into the contested West Philippine Sea, Graham said. Apart from maritime training, Teodoro said there will be more aerial, land, cyber, and multidomain training exercises between Filipino and Australian troops. Military officials told Defense News that Army training has been a priority area for the Australian military’s training playbook in the Philippines. The focus follows sweeping changes in both countries’ land forces to prepare them for modern conflicts. While the Philippine Army expands from its signature jungle and urban warfare expertise toward coastal defense, the Australian ground service has pivoted toward littoral warfare. Since 2023, exchanges have focused on techniques, tactics, and procedures for amphibious operations, Army spokesperson Col. Louie Dema-ala told Defense News. But future iterations will include advanced training, Dema-ala said. “We are transitioning into a multi-domain capable Army.” The exchange is not one-sided. Australia also stands to benefit from the Philippine Army’s experience operating in dense jungle terrain. “This is not just a one-way process. We can learn from the jungle warfare fighting skills, and I think that’s important to stress. No one can tell us about the Philippines better than the Filipinos,” Graham said.

title: General Flash raises $128 million to scale US critical metals production
zh_title: General Flash 筹集 1.28 亿美元以扩大美国关键金属生产
summary: 总部位于马萨诸塞州剑桥的初创公司 General Flash 周二宣布，已在种子轮和 A 轮融资中筹集了 1.28 亿美元的股权资本，以扩大对国家安全至关重要的关键金属的国内生产。投资者包括 Lux Capital、Construct Capital、Overmatch Ventures、GreatPoint Ventures、Pillar VC、Lowercarbon Capital、Ensemble VC、Ravelin 和领先的天使投资者。钨、钛、锆、钽和稀土等关键金属是半导体、国防、航空航天和先进制造的重要组成部分。 20世纪，美国
content:
总部位于马萨诸塞州剑桥的初创公司 General Flash 周二宣布，已在种子轮和 A 轮融资中筹集了 1.28 亿美元的股权资本，以扩大对国家安全至关重要的关键金属的国内生产。投资者包括 Lux Capital、Construct Capital、Overmatch Ventures、GreatPoint Ventures、Pillar VC、Lowercarbon Capital、Ensemble VC、Ravelin 和领先的天使投资者。钨、钛、锆、钽和稀土等关键金属是半导体、国防、航空航天和先进制造的重要组成部分。 20世纪，美国开发了大部分用于制造这些材料的技术，但允许生产转移到海外，而如今它严重依赖外国供应，其中中国占炼油能力的80%以上。从 2027 年 1 月 1 日开始，战争部规定将禁止中国从美国国防供应链供应许多此类关键材料。美国国防部联邦采购法规补充条款 (DFARS) 制定的规则规定，任何向国防部提供商品、服务或技术的主承包商或分包商都必须遵守这些标准。金属氧化物转化 General Flash 表示，其工艺将金属氧化物直接转化为高纯度、半导体级金属，且不产生任何排放。该公司表示，它比传统炼油速度更快、成本更低，并为美国提供了
这是一种在国内建立具有成本效益的精炼能力，而不是依赖外国供应的方法。该公司表示，其金属化工艺将从麻省理工学院附近的试验线扩大到 2027 年每年 1,000 吨的商业生产。其固态闪蒸电解 (SSFE) 工艺与金属无关，可用于精炼钨、钽、钛、铪、锆、锗、钇、铌、钼和稀土元素。该公司表示，这笔资金将支持到 2027 年夏季进行商业规模生产，该工厂将成为世界上最大、最先进的关键材料生产工厂之一。 General Flash 首席执行官、麻省理工学院材料科学与工程系访问委员会成员、麻省理工中心研究科学家 Ric Fulop 在一份新闻稿中表示：“关键金属是每个先进行业的基础。” “我们创办 General Flash 是因为我们相信有更好、更清洁、更高效的方法来制造这些材料。我们已经在麻省理工学院附近的多吨试点工厂进行了演示，这笔资金完全资助我们在美国第一家大型工厂的生产。”    Lux Capital 合伙人彼得·赫伯特 (Peter Hebert) 表示：“每个先进行业都依赖关键金属，而我们制造这些金属的方式几十年来几乎没有改变。” “General Flash 拥有经过中试规模验证的真正新工艺，并且其创始人之前曾创建并扩大过一家制造公司。
我们相信它可以成为未来十年美国重要的工业公司之一。”

【原文 English Original】
Cambridge, Massachusetts-based startup General Flash announced Tuesday it has raised $128 million in equity capital across its Seed and Series A rounds to scale domestic production of critical metals essential to national security.   Investors include Lux Capital, Construct Capital, Overmatch Ventures, GreatPoint Ventures, Pillar VC, Lowercarbon Capital, Ensemble VC, Ravelin and leading angel investors. Critical metals such as tungsten, titanium, zirconium, tantalum and rare earths are vital components in semiconductors, defense, aerospace and advanced manufacturing. In the 20th century, the US developed most of the techniques used to make these materials but allowed production to move overseas, and today it depends heavily on foreign supply, with China accounting for more than 80% of refining capacity. Starting January 1, 2027, Department of War rules will bar Chinese supply for many of these critical materials from U.S. defense supply chains. Rules set by the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) stipulates any prime contractor or subcontractor supplying goods, services, or technology to the DoW must follow these standards.   Metal oxides conversion      General Flash said its process converts metal oxides directly into high-purity, semiconductor-grade metal, with no emissions. The company said it is faster and lower cost than conventional refining and gives the U.S. a way to build cost-effective refining capacity at home instead of relying on foreign supply.   The company said its process for metallization will scale from its pilot line near MIT to 1,000 metric tons per year of commercial production in 2027.   Its Solid-State Flash Electrolysis (SSFE) process is metal-agnostic and can be used to refine materials like tungsten, tantalum, titanium, hafnium, zirconium, germanium, yttrium, niobium, molybdenum, and rare earth elements.    The funding will support commercial-scale production by Summer 2027, in what will be one of the largest and most advanced critical materials production plants in the world, the company said.    “Critical metals are foundational to every advanced industry,” General Flash CEO and member of the visiting committee of the MIT Department of Materials Science and Engineering and research scientist at the MIT Center Ric Fulop said in a news release.   “We started General Flash because we believe there’s a better, cleaner and more efficient way to make these materials. We’ve already demonstrated it at our multi-ton pilot facility near MIT, and this funding fully finances production of our first large plant in the U.S.”    “Every advanced industry runs on critical metals, and the way we make them has barely changed in decades,” Lux Capital Partner Peter Hebert said. “General Flash has a genuinely new process, proven at pilot scale, and a founder who has built and scaled a manufacturing company before. We believe it can become one of the important American industrial companies of the next decade.”

title: Canada widens tariff relief on Chinese metals
zh_title: 加拿大扩大对中国金属的关税减免
summary: 随着加拿大总理马克·卡尼扩大与北京的贸易协定，加拿大将扩大对国内供应短缺的中国钢铁和铝产品的关税减免，并将现有豁免延长至 2028 年。加拿大联邦政府周二在卡尼在深圳会见国家主席习近平后表示，此次扩大涵盖了加拿大供应不足或无法获得的23种钢铁和9种铝关税商品的全部或部分。作为交换，中国将对加拿大约 4 亿美元（2.8 亿美元）的猪肉、鱼类和海鲜出口提供额外关税减免。 “加拿大和中国已经重新
content:
随着加拿大总理马克·卡尼扩大与北京的贸易协定，加拿大将扩大对国内供应短缺的中国钢铁和铝产品的关税减免，并将现有豁免延长至 2028 年。加拿大联邦政府周二在卡尼在深圳会见国家主席习近平后表示，此次扩大涵盖了加拿大供应不足或无法获得的23种钢铁和9种铝关税商品的全部或部分。作为交换，中国将对加拿大约 4 亿美元（2.8 亿美元）的猪肉、鱼类和海鲜出口提供额外关税减免。卡尼在一份声明中表示：“加拿大和中国已经重新调整了我们的关系，以造福两国公民。”周二宣布的协议降低了无法在国内采购足够特定金属的加拿大制造商的进口成本，同时保留了旨在保护加拿大生产的更广泛的关税框架。渥太华对中国钢铁和铝的更广泛关税仍然有效。美国的要求 美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔 (Jamieson Greer) 在 8 月 26 日接受 CBC 采访时警告称，加拿大钢铁和铝的关税减免需要采取保障措施，防止外国金属通过加拿大进入美国市场。他说，华盛顿希望渥太华调整其贸易保护措施，以防止出现这种情况。白宫贸易和制造政策办公室在八月份的逃税评估中将加拿大列为中国“最大推动者”之一。
该办公室称，中国出口商通过第三国运送货物，并谎报其原产地，以获得较低的美国关税。加拿大以威胁国内生产和投资的非市场政策和做法为由，于 2024 年 10 月对特定的中国进口钢铁和铝征收 25% 的附加税。该措施仍然是渥太华金属关税制度的一部分，此外还有涉及钢铁进口配额和含有原产于中国的金属的商品的单独规则。这些豁免被称为减免，减轻了进口商对合格产品的关税。财政部表示，现有的特定产品减免适用于所列商品的所有进口商，而产品未涵盖的企业可以申请特殊减免。一月协议 最新措施以各国一月贸易安排为基础。此前的减免涵盖了 66 个产品特定减免项目和 49 个公司特定关税项目减免。加拿大全球事务部在一份背景声明中表示，根据该安排，渥太华还增加了七种钢铁、两种铝和四种钢铁衍生产品的承保范围。新的两年延期将现有金属减免的期限从 2026 年底推迟到 2028 年底。渥太华将额外的 32 个关税项目与加拿大供应缺口挂钩。领导人的声明并未具体指明哪些制造商将从中受益。更广泛的解冻也会影响电池供应链。
加拿大1月份与中国达成的协议规定了49,000辆中国电动汽车的初始配额，关税为6.1%。加拿大全球事务部表示，自3月份以来，已有约16,200辆汽车根据该协议进入加拿大。卡尼另外表示，加拿大将于 2027 年向中国派遣贸易代表团。渥太华表示，新的关系已恢复了 90% 以上的加拿大贸易准入，此前受关税行动影响，出口额近 75 亿美元。

【原文 English Original】
Canada will expand tariff relief on Chinese steel and aluminum products in short supply at home and extend existing exemptions through 2028, as Prime Minister Mark Carney broadens a trade accord with Beijing. The expansion covers all or part of 23 steel and nine aluminum tariff items for which Canadian supply is insufficient or unavailable, Canada’s federal government said Tuesday after Carney met President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. In exchange, China will provide additional tariff relief on about $400 million (US$280 million) in Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports. “Canada and China have recalibrated our relationship to the benefit of citizens in both countries,” Carney said in a statement. The agreement announced Tuesday eases import costs for Canadian manufacturers that cannot source enough of the specified metals domestically, while preserving the wider tariff framework intended to protect Canadian production. Ottawa’s broader duties on Chinese steel and aluminum remain in place. U.S. demand U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned in an Aug. 26 CBC interview that tariff relief for Canadian steel and aluminum would require safeguards against foreign metals entering the American market through Canada. Washington wanted Ottawa to align its trade protections to prevent that route, he said. The White House’s Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy named Canada among China’s “biggest enablers” in an August assessment of tariff evasion. Chinese exporters were routing goods through third countries and misrepresenting their origin to obtain lower U.S. duties, the office alleged. Canada imposed a 25% surtax on specified Chinese steel and aluminum imports in October 2024, citing non-market policies and practices that threatened domestic production and investment. The measure remains part of Ottawa’s metals tariff system, alongside separate rules covering steel import quotas and goods containing metal originally made in China. The exemptions, known as remissions, relieve importers of duties on qualifying products. Existing product-specific relief applies to all importers of the listed goods, while businesses whose products are not covered can request exceptional relief, the Department of Finance says. January accord The latest measures build on the countries’ January trade arrangement. Earlier relief covered 66 lines of product-specific remissions and 49 tariff lines of company-specific remissions. Ottawa also added coverage for seven steel, two aluminum and four steel derivative products under that arrangement, Global Affairs Canada said in a background statement. The new two-year extension moves the expiry of existing metals relief from the end of 2026 to the end of 2028. Ottawa tied the additional 32 tariff items to gaps in Canadian supply. The leaders’ announcement didn’t identify individual manufacturers that would benefit. The broader thaw also affects the battery supply chain. Canada’s January arrangement with China set an initial quota for 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles at a 6.1% tariff. About 16,200 vehicles have entered Canada under the arrangement since March, Global Affairs Canada said. Separately, Carney said Canada would conduct a trade mission to China in 2027. The renewed relationship has restored access for more than 90% of Canadian trade previously affected by tariff action, representing nearly $7.5 billion in exports, Ottawa says.

title: AI safety legislation has a conflict-of-interest problem — Big US labs are warning of risk just as cheaper Chinese open-weight models erode their commercial edge
zh_title: 人工智能安全立法存在利益冲突问题——美国大型实验室警告风险，就像更便宜的中国开放重量模型侵蚀其商业优势一样
summary: 在没有黄仁勋的 Nvidia 中，人工智能模型和出口管制之争仍在继续。但谁控制了芯片的流向，也就控制了领先的前沿人工智能模型的流向。据报道，OpenAI 现在支持美国国会两党共同推动限制中国获得先进人工智能加速器和设备。但额外的人工智能安全问题是否真实存在，或者它们也是巩固其在快速发展的行业顶端地位的便捷方式？我们采访了欧洲开放市场研究所所长马克斯·冯·图恩 (Max von Thun) 等专家，以了解更多信息。首先，我们来看看 OpenAI 的 GP
content:
在没有黄仁勋的 Nvidia 中，人工智能模型和出口管制之争仍在继续。但谁控制了芯片的流向，也就控制了领先的前沿人工智能模型的流向。据报道，OpenAI 现在支持美国国会两党共同推动限制中国获得先进人工智能加速器和设备。但额外的人工智能安全问题是否真实存在，或者它们也是巩固其在快速发展的行业顶端地位的便捷方式？我们采访了欧洲开放市场研究所所长马克斯·冯·图恩 (Max von Thun) 等专家，以了解更多信息。首先，我们以 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 为例。该公司于 9 月份推出了该模型，并声称这是该公司迄今为止功能最强大、协调性最好的系统。 OpenAI 自己的测试表明，Astra 在遵循指令和尊重边界方面表现得更好。在一项内部计算机使用安全基准中，不一致结果的比例从 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 18.8% 下降到 Astra 的 3.4%。但仅仅因为它表面上表现更好并不意味着它完全安全。 OpenAI 表示，当他们测试 Astra 逃避监管的能力时，其书面推理比其前身更难监控。该模型开始识别自己何时被观看，并改变其解释以适应研究，从而更难判断它何时实际上在做他们不想要的事情。这是人工智能对齐专家需要尝试解决的一个经典问题。
确保事物安全 多年来，开发人员一直依靠监控人工智能模型的思想链（其书面工作）来了解它在做什么。但是，如果日益强大的人工智能模型能够更好地隐藏其推理过程，那么这种监督就会变得更加困难。 OpenAI 表示，Astra 在执行复杂任务时仍然难以隐藏推理，其评估结果表明其具有很强的整体一致性，但这里存在令人担忧的权衡迹象。当人工智能系统的部署具有更大的自主权时，这些令人担忧的迹象变得更加明显。 7 月，OpenAI 模型绕过了其内部评估限制，获得了对属于 Hugging Face 的研究基础设施和受损系统的访问权限，以及澳大利亚和加拿大政府控制的 IT 系统的访问权限。为了方便而进行安全打击？在此背景下，呼吁采取更强有力的安全措施似乎完全合理。但欧洲开放市场研究所所长马克斯·冯·图恩认为，这场辩论有可能忽视令人不安的利益冲突。 “我认为很多关于人工智能安全的观点都是非常真诚的，”他在接受 Tom's Hardware Premium 采访时说道。但他认为，商业考虑因素非常重要。
像 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 这样的公司正在花费巨资开发和部署模型，同时面临着这样的问题：它们的竞争优势是否能够在功能日益强大、成本更低的替代方案的出现中幸存下来——特别是当它们走出去并通过 IPO 寻求公众资金时。“即使它们已经获得了大量用户，它们也没有巨大的护城河，”von Thun 说。 “他们绝对是脆弱的。”这些漏洞正变得越来越明显。 Mozilla 9 月份的一份报告估计，美国领先的封闭式模型与其开放式重量竞争对手之间的能力差距已缩小至仅四个月多一点。这很重要，因为开放权重模型让人们可以自由地不依赖公司的订阅服务。他们

【原文 English Original】
The battle for AI models and export controls continues amidst a Jensen Huang-free Nvidia. But who controls the flow of chips also controls the flow of leading frontier AI models. OpenAI reportedly now supports a bipartisan push in the U.S. Congress to restrict China's access to advanced AI accelerators and equipment. But are the additional AI safety concerns genuine, or are they also a convenient way to shore up its position at the top of a fast-moving industry? We speak to experts like Max von Thun, director of Open Markets Institute Europe, to find out more. First off, let's take OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. The company launched the model in September with eye-popping claims that it was the firm’s most capable and best-aligned system yet. OpenAI’s own testing suggested that Astra was much better at following instructions and respecting boundaries. In one internal computer-use safety benchmark, the proportion of misaligned outcomes fell from 18.8% with GPT-5.6 Sol to 3.4% with Astra. But just because it was better behaved on the surface didn’t mean it was entirely safe. OpenAI said Astra’s written reasoning was harder to monitor than its predecessor’s when they were testing its ability to evade oversight. The model began to recognize when it was being watched and altered its explanations to suit the study, making it harder to tell when it was actually doing something they didn’t want. It’s a classic problem for AI alignment experts to try and resolve. Keeping things safe For years, developers have relied on monitoring an AI model's chain of thought — its written working — to understand what it is doing. But if increasingly powerful AI models become better at hiding their reasoning processes, that oversight becomes harder to do. OpenAI says that Astra still struggles to hide reasoning when it’s carrying out complex tasks, and its evaluation results suggest it has strong overall alignment, but there are worrying signs of a trade-off here. Those worrying signs become even more so when AI systems are being deployed with more autonomy. In July, OpenAI models ducked its internal evaluation restrictions to gain access to research infrastructure and compromised systems belonging to Hugging Face, and to IT systems controlled by the Australian and Canadian governments. Safety crackdowns for convenience? Against that backdrop, calls for stronger safety measures seem entirely reasonable. But Max von Thun, director of Open Markets Institute Europe, believes the debate risks overlooking an uncomfortable conflict of interest. "I think a lot of these views about AI safety are very genuinely held," he told Tom’s Hardware Premium in an interview. But commercial considerations loom large, he reckons. Companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are spending huge sums developing and deploying models, while facing questions about whether their competitive advantages can survive the arrival of increasingly capable, cheaper alternatives — particularly as they go out and seek funding from the public through an IPO . "They don't have huge moats, even if they’ve acquired a lot of users,” von Thun said. “They’re definitely vulnerable.” Those vulnerabilities are becoming increasingly obvious. A September report from Mozilla estimated the capability gap between leading closed American models and their open-weight competitors had narrowed to just over four months. That matters because open-weight models give people the freedom not to rely on a company’s subscription services. They can be deployed on infrastructure controlled by the customer, modified for specialised tasks, and operated at lower costs. But to the discomfort of U.S. companies, many of them are based in China. And it’s at that point that AI safety gets muddled with geopolitics. China versus the U.S. In July, Axios reported that OpenAI and Anthropic, despite their fierce commercial rivalry, had found a common cause: warning U.S. policymakers about the dangers of powerful Chinese open-weight models. Kristy Loke, an AI governance researcher at King's College London who specialises in China's approach to the technology, questions the timing. "It's very suspicious timing asking for pacing," she told Tom's Hardware Premium , referring to calls for slowing frontier AI development just as Chinese open-weight models are undercutting their American rivals on price. Loke believes companies genuinely worry about the risks. But she also thinks they're worried about their commercial prospects. "they're calling for pacing because they have some safety concerns, they have some commercial anxiety," she said. She believes some influential people in American AI have increasingly sought to "paint open models in a very bad light", portraying them as inherently less secure than closed alternatives. Yet the risks of AI systems misbehaving aren't restricted to models developed in China, as OpenAI's own incidents demonstrate. But open-weight models come with their own risks. Because their underlying parameters can be modified , third parties can create and distribute "abliterated" models, removing the refusal behaviours designed to prevent AI from responding to potentially harmful requests. Many of these models are available on platforms including Hugging Face. “They’re not adding in new behaviour; they’re just removing this refusal behaviour,” said Catherine Flick, professor of ethics and games technology at the University of Staffordshire, in an interview with Tom’s Hardware Premium . Abliterating models doesn’t make them more capable, Flick said, but it does mean they can answer questions they previously wouldn’t have been willing to. That also means those responses might not have been tested for accuracy or hallucinations. Those in favour of open-weight models like DeepSeek and Qwen say that removing those guardrails helps security researchers understand how AI behaves. Flick said that’s plausible, but “I just don’t really buy it,” she said. She reckons that the negative potential outputs outweigh the positive case for abliteration because when they’re publicly available, preventing their misuse becomes tricky. American labs clearly have commercial reasons to criticise open-weight competitors because the latter undercuts their economics, but it also doesn’t mean their concerns about safety aren’t valid, too. Von Thun fears that could result in precisely the wrong kind of regulation. "I think what we should not be doing is allowing the companies to basically form a safety cartel," he said. Yet U.S. AI companies benefit from the government's determination to maintain its advantage over China. Von Thun argues the Trump administration has created an environment in which economic power translates into political influence, allowing major technology companies to invoke national security concerns when arguing for policies that may also serve their commercial interests. But that could backfire. "I think completely closing off the market to AI products from other countries, including China, would not be the right approach," von Thun said. China’s own alignment approach Part of the reason that wouldn’t be the right approach is that the idea that the United States is focused on developing AI responsibly while China isn’t is a fallacy. Just earlier this month, Reuters reported that ByteDance had established a dedicated Alignment & Preparedness team, recruiting researchers to investigate safety risks arising from increasingly capable AI systems. For von Thun, the solution is to prevent either industry or geopolitical competition from determining what safety means. He points to the European Union's AI Act, which establishes obligations for developers of general-purpose AI models classified as posing systemic risks. The obligations require companies to conduct model evaluations, adversarial testing, cybersecurity measures and also to report serious incidents. The opposition to the EU’s AI Act from American tech companies, U.S. politicians and the general public who grouse about the way it delays access to cutting-edge models for Europe’s 450 million citizens demonstrates that these provisions don't automatically solve the alignment problem. But they at least involve more people in the conversation about what is and isn’t acceptable for AI than just the industry's biggest participants. Watching watchdogs Even when AI companies agree to independent oversight, they still want some say over how it works — and their own internal decision-making on what is and isn’t safe differs from that of those outside the company. Loke warns that leading AI companies are experimenting with recursive self-improvement, where models help develop their successors, potentially making it more difficult for humans to understand how decisions are being made. "They’re still attempting more risky methods to train AI that will make the AI harder to control," she said. Von Thun also believes competition rules and interoperability requirements could help prevent AI companies from locking customers into proprietary ecosystems as their agents become increasingly embedded in everyday workflows. There are plenty of good reasons to be concerned about alignment, particularly when the models being developed are becoming more capable and more difficult to monitor. But letting the companies responsible for building them determine what constitutes an acceptable risk, and who can compete, brings its own dangers. “I’m not saying we don’t need to worry about safety,” said von Thun, “but we should about letting the companies do it."

title: Taipei 101 lit up in support of Jensen Huang
zh_title: 台北101亮灯支持黄仁勋
summary: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职后，台湾的一座摩天大楼成为了一系列支持这位被罢免的创始人的信息的背景，这位被罢黜的创始人承认与一名被指控为中国政府间谍的女性有染。此后，美国政府宣布对这名女子所在的公司 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，原因是担心该公司可能帮助违反了与 Nvidia AI 芯片相关的出口管制。尽管如此，据中央通讯社报道，11 月 10 日晚上，台北 101 大楼的外部投射了信息
content:
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职后，台湾的一座摩天大楼成为了一系列支持这位被罢免的创始人的信息的背景，这位被罢黜的创始人承认与一名被指控为中国政府间谍的女性有染。此后，美国政府宣布对这名女子所在的公司 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，原因是担心该公司可能帮助违反了与 Nvidia AI 芯片相关的出口管制。尽管如此，据中央通讯社报道，11 月 16 日晚，台北 101 大楼的外部投射了信息。这些信息包括“台湾 ♡ 詹森”、“家庭 ♡ 友谊”和“共同成长”，其驱动力可能是黄在该国近乎名人般的知名度。这种名人地位让台湾民众对黄的同情心不断增长，台湾科技行业的人士齐心协力为该项目提供资金。据报道，一名科技人员表示，这次灯光秀是为了“带回黄仁勋”，表达台湾的关切。台北 101 大楼亮灯支持丑闻缠身的黄仁勋 周一晚上，台北 101 大楼亮起支持黄仁勋的信息，几天前，黄仁勋因婚外情被曝光，国家安全问题受到越来越多的关注，辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。 https://t.co/VOtX1RX5qN 2026 年 11 月 16 日 这种担忧可能不需要太久了。
最近的报道表明，黄仁勋在递交辞呈几天后，可能正在密谋重返英伟达最高职位。SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 已经大力支持黄仁勋重返英伟达的想法。迫使英伟达董事会下手的呼声也蔓延到了白宫，美国总统特朗普也呼吁让这位前首席执行官复职。尽管他的爱人是否是中国间谍，以及如果是的话，黄对这一事实可能了解多少，仍然存在不确定性。然而，特朗普表示，黄没有将国家安全置于危险之中。就其本身而言，据信英伟达董事会不会认真考虑允许黄继续他辞职前留下的工作。一位消息人士告诉 CNBC，该公司正专注于调查黄的行为和国家安全调查，而不是讨论他的回归。毫无疑问，这项调查还将考虑有关黄仁勋另一起婚外情的报道，这次是与英伟达高管。目前，英伟达前首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)担任临时首席执行官。克雷斯没过多久就迎来了第一个重大考验——丑闻发生以来该公司的首次财报电话会议将于今天（11 月 17 日）举行。

【原文 English Original】
Following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , a Taiwanese skyscraper became the backdrop for a series of messages in support of the ousted founder, who admitted to having an affair with a woman who has been accused of being a spy for the Chinese government . The U.S. government has since announced a criminal investigation into the company the woman worked for, Megaspeed, over concerns it may have aided in the breaking of export controls related to Nvidia AI chips. Despite that fact, CNA reports that the Taipei 101 building saw messages projected onto its exterior on the night of November 16. The messages included “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” and “Thrive Together,” with the driving force likely to be Huang's almost celebrity-like level of fame in the country. That celebrity status has seen public sympathy for Huang grow within Taiwan, with people within the country's technology industry coming together to fund the project. One technology worker reportedly said that the light show was supposed to “bring back Jensen Huang” and show Taiwan's concern. Taipei 101 lights up in support of scandal-hit Jensen HuangTaipei 101 lit up with messages of support for Jensen Huang on Monday evening, days after he resigned as Nvidia CEO amid revelations about his extramarital affairs & mounting scrutiny over national security concerns. https://t.co/VOtX1RX5qN November 16, 2026 That concern may not be needed for too much longer. Recent reports suggest that Huang could be plotting a return to the top job at Nvidia just days after he handed in his resignation. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have already thrown their weight behind the idea of Huang's return to Nvidia. The clamor to force the hand of Nvidia's board has also extended to the White House, with U.S. President Trump also calling for the former CEO to be reinstated . This is despite ongoing uncertainty over whether his love interest was a Chinese spy and, if so, how much Huang may have known about that fact. Trump, however, says that Huang did not put national security at risk. For its part, it isn't believed that the Nvidia board is seriously considering allowing Huang to pick up where he left off pre-resignation. A source told CNBC that the company is focused on investigating Huang's conduct and a national security investigation and is not discussing his return. That investigation will no doubt also consider reports that Huang had another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive . For now, Nvidia's former CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO. Kress hasn't had long to settle in ahead of the first big test — the company's first earnings call since the scandal will take place today, November 17.

title: US government confirms criminal investigation into Singapore company at the heart of Jensen Huang scandal
zh_title: 美国政府确认对黄仁勋丑闻核心新加坡公司进行刑事调查
summary: 美国司法部和商务部已确认对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，并发表联合声明称，他们将“对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。当局认为，Megaspeed 是众多可能规避出口规则的公司之一，这些规则旨在限制向经批准的公司和国家销售先进的人工智能芯片，例如英伟达制造的芯片。该公司是最近黄仁勋丑闻的核心，他上周从该公司辞职。高迪
content:
美国司法部和商务部已确认对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，并发表联合声明称，他们将“对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁”。当局认为，Megaspeed 是众多可能规避出口规则的公司之一，这些规则旨在限制向经批准的公司和国家销售先进的人工智能芯片，例如英伟达制造的芯片。该公司是最近黄仁勋丑闻的核心，他上周从该公司辞职。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：tsmc） 虽然美国在芯片制裁上反复无常，但中国正在建立自己的芯片供应市场 中国长达十年的半导体推动状况 华为 Ascend NPU 路线图审查了中国长鑫存储的目标，到 2030 年，第六座大型晶圆厂将占据 30% 的 DRAM 内存市场份额 中国最新一轮稀土出口管制解释说，Megaspeed 已被添加到 Nvidia 的禁售名单中声明显示，该清单将于 2025 年 6 月列入清单，但《纽约时报》的一篇报道称，马来西亚 Megaspeed 子公司在该日期后整整八个月内继续收到大量 Nvidia 芯片。据信，英伟达受出口管制的 Blackwell 和 H200 芯片是通过第三方或直接从英伟达本身运往 Speedmatrix，然后再转交给中国。
Nvidia 辩称，它已获得美国商务部的许可，可以向 Megaspeed 运送组件。值得注意的是，Nvidia 继续将 Megaspeed 列为云合作伙伴。商务部于 2024 年首次启动对 Megaspeed 的调查，原因是其可能存在出口违规行为，随后展开了新的刑事调查。到 2025 年 5 月，它已要求英伟达提供与其向 Megaspeed 销售相关的数据，到 6 月，官员们访问了 Megaspeed，甚至采访了据称是中国间谍的现任前高管 Alice Huang。黄女士也是时任英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在本月初辞职前曾有过外遇的女性。在那次访问之后，司法部牵头对 Megaspeed 进行了调查。商务部和司法部关于 Megaspeed 调查的联合声明。 https://t.co/aAdtN9aDfF 2026 年 11 月 17 日 Megaspeed 长期以来一直被指控为人工智​​能组件走私活动的幌子。 2025 年 10 月，一项调查声称，该公司通过进口然后再出口到中国，帮助将价值约 20 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国。 Megaspeed 表示，公司遵守所有法律，而且风流丑闻的核心女性黄女士已不再在公司工作。中国政府也驳回了有关她是国家间谍的说法。
商务部和司法部的联合声明指出，迄今为止，该公司在起诉芯片走私者方面有着良好的记录。迄今为止，在总共六项调查中，已有 17 名被告受到指控，而且可能还会有更多被告受到指控。一名加州男子最近因被指控向中国走私价值超过 3 亿美元的受出口限制的 Nvidia 芯片而被捕。他现在面临最高20年的监禁。

【原文 English Original】
A criminal investigation into Megaspeed has been confirmed by the United States Justice and Commerce Departments, with a joint statement saying that they will “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred.” Authorities believe that Megaspeed is one of a raft of companies that may have circumvented export rules designed to limit the sale of advanced AI chips, like those built by Nvidia, to approved companies and countries. The company is at the heart of the recent Jensen Huang scandal, which saw him resign from the company last week . Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained Megaspeed was added to Nvidia's no-sell list in June 2025, the statement reveals, but a New York Times report claims that a Malaysian Megaspeed subsidiary continued to receive large shipments of Nvidia chips for a full eight months after that date. It's believed that Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell and H200 chips were shipped to Speedmatrix, either via third parties or directly from Nvidia itself, before being handed off to China. Nvidia has argued that it was given Commerce Department permission to ship the components to Megaspeed. Notably, Nvidia continues to list Megaspeed as a cloud partner. The new criminal investigation follows a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed that first kicked off in 2024 over possible export violations. By May 2025, it had requested Nvidia's data relating to sales it made to Megaspeed, and by June, officials visited Megaspeed and even interviewed Alice Huang, the now-former executive who is allegedly a Chinese spy . Ms. Huang is also the woman that then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with before resigning his position earlier this month . Following that visit, the Justice Department took the lead in the investigation into Megaspeed. Joint Statement from Department of Commerce and Department of Justice on Megaspeed Investigation. https://t.co/aAdtN9aDfF November 17, 2026 Megaspeed has long been accused of being a front for an AI component smuggling operation. In October 2025, an investigation claimed that it had helped move around $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China by importing them and then re-exporting them to the country. Megaspeed says that it complies with all laws and that the woman at the center of the affair scandal, Ms. Huang, is no longer at the company. The Chinese government has also dismissed claims that she was a state spy. The joint Commerce and Justice Departments' statement pointed to its strong track record when prosecuting chip smugglers to date. 17 defendants across a total of six investigations have been charged so far, with more likely to follow. A Californian man was recently arrested after being accused of smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-restricted Nvidia chips to China. He now faces up to 20 years in prison.

title: Nvidia board establishes National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee in wake of Jensen Huang scandal
zh_title: 黄仁勋丑闻发生后，英伟达董事会成立国家安全和出口管制监督委员会
summary: 黄仁勋从公司辞职后不到一周，英伟达董事会就成立了自己的国家安全和出口管制监督委员会。根据其公告，新的常务委员会将对英伟达的“国家安全政策、出口管制合规和全球贸易风险管理”进行高层监督，其国家安全团队和全球贸易合规团队直接向该集团和临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯报告。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：tsmc）而美国在芯片制裁方面却摇摆不定
content:
黄仁勋从公司辞职后不到一周，英伟达董事会就成立了自己的国家安全和出口管制监督委员会。根据其公告，新的常务委员会将对英伟达的“国家安全政策、出口管制合规和全球贸易风险管理”进行高层监督，其国家安全团队和全球贸易合规团队直接向该集团和临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯报告。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：台积电） 虽然美国在芯片制裁上反复无常，但中国正在建立自己的芯片供应市场 中国长达十年的半导体发展状况 华为 Ascend NPU 路线图审查了中国长鑫存储的目标，到 2030 年，第六座大型晶圆厂将占据 30% 的 DRAM 内存市场份额 中国最新一轮稀土出口管制解释道英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯表示：“超级智能给国家安全带来了前所未有的挑战。” “作为全球领先的先进计算公司，Nvidia 有责任也有机会引领行业应对这些挑战。
我们致力于与政府和行业合作伙伴进行建设性合作，帮助建立和推进一个强有力的框架，利用我们掌握的一切工具来维护国家安全，同时支持持续的技术创新。”黄仁勋与被指控为中国间谍的黄爱丽丝（Alice Huang）有染的传言使该公司陷入混乱，尤其是在他承认并随后道歉之后。人们开始挖掘黄仁勋的详细信息，透露她处于错综复杂的公司网络的中心，据报道，她在将价值约 75 亿美元的被禁 Nvidia 芯片进口到中国方面发挥了重要作用。更深入的调查还显示，她的丈夫康伟是她声名鹊起的幕后黑手，并且似乎接受了她与这位亿万富翁的关系。目前尚不清楚这对夫妇做出这些精明的商业举动是否纯粹是为了利润，还是受到隐藏的第三方的控制，但这无疑使该公司面临更多审查。此后，众议院中国、外交和情报委员会主席邀请詹森参加闭门简报会，讨论英伟达的“针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议”，而唐纳德·特朗普总统则提到联邦调查局正在调查黄仁勋与黄女士的关系。美国
2022年，美国首次对英伟达最先进的芯片A100和H100实施出口管制，迫使该公司生产符合华盛顿性能限制的中国市场A800和H800 GPU。然而，白宫在2023年再次降低了标准，导致H20的价格更加淡化，但需求量仍然很高。尽管特朗普政府没有实施拜登的人工智能扩散规则，该规则威胁要彻底禁止多个国家购买英伟达人工智能芯片，但总统最终从 2025 年 4 月至 6 月禁止向中国出口 H20 芯片。甚至在特朗普全面禁止英伟达人工智能 GPU 之前，已经有多起走私报告，一家半导体分析公司追踪了超过 1.5 吉瓦出口到中国的被禁人工智能芯片，并估计多达 150 万块英伟达 GPU 被走私。近年来走私。德斯普

【原文 English Original】
Less than a week after Jensen Huang resigned from the company , Nvidia's board has created its own National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. According to its announcement , the new standing committee will provide high-level oversight of Nvidia’s “national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management,” with its National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team reporting directly to the group and to interim CEO Colette Kress. Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained “Nvidia recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security,” Nvidia chairperson Harvey Jones said. “As the world’s leading advanced computing company, Nvidia has both a responsibility and an opportunity to lead the industry in addressing these challenges. We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation.” The rumors of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, have thrown the company into turmoil, especially after his admission and subsequent apology . People have begun digging into details about Ms. Huang, revealing that she was at the center of a tangled web of companies and was reportedly instrumental in importing around $7.5 billion of banned Nvidia chips into China. A deeper investigation also revealed that her husband, Kang Wei, was behind her rise to prominence and seemingly accepted her relationship with the billionaire. It remains unclear if the couple made these shrewd business moves purely for profit or if they were under the control of a hidden third party, but it has certainly exposed the company to additional scrutiny. The chairpersons of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence have since invited Jensen to a closed-door briefing to discuss Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage,” while President Donald Trump mentioned that the FBI is looking into Jensen Huang’s relationship with Ms. Huang. The U.S. first applied export controls to Nvidia’s most advanced chips, the A100 and H100, in 2022, forcing the company to create the China-market A800 and H800 GPUs that complied with Washington’s performance limitations. However, the White House lowered the bar once more in 2023, which resulted in the even more watered-down H20, which, nonetheless, remained in high demand. Even though the Trump administration did not implement Biden’s AI diffusion rule, which threatened to outright ban several countries from buying Nvidia AI chips, the president eventually banned the export of H20 chips to China from April to June 2025. Even before Trump’s total Nvidia AI GPU ban, there have already been multiple reports of smuggling, with one semiconductor analysis firm tracking more than 1.5 gigawatts of banned AI chips exported to China and estimating that up to 1.5 million Nvidia GPUs were smuggled in recent years. Despite that, the former Nvidia chief has always denied the allegations, saying that “ There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion. ” Whether the allegations are true or not, it seems that the company is taking the situation seriously and taking steps to plug any leaks. As for Jensen Huang, he may be out of the company, but he still has to face Congress and all ongoing investigations.

title: Satellite imagery reveals vegetation recovery at solar plant in semi-arid region of China
zh_title: 卫星图像揭示中国半干旱地区太阳能发电厂植被恢复情况
summary: 中国河海大学的研究人员对位于中国青海省海南藏族自治州共和县的21吉瓦共和塔拉坦太阳能电站的季节性植被变化进行了研究，发现光伏安装两年内植被水平就超过了施工前的水平。该地区地势平坦，平均海拔约 2,920 米，气候寒冷、干旱至半干旱。年平均气温4.1℃，年降水量303毫米，其中近88%集中在5月至5月之间。
content:
中国河海大学的研究人员对位于中国青海省海南藏族自治州共和县的21吉瓦共和塔拉坦太阳能电站的季节性植被变化进行了研究，发现光伏安装两年内植被水平就超过了施工前的水平。该地区地势平坦，平均海拔约 2,920 米，气候寒冷、干旱至半干旱。年平均气温4.1℃，年降水量303毫米，其中近88%集中在5月至9月之间。年蒸发量约为 1,800 毫米，该地区每年的日照时间超过 2,900 小时，并经历显着的风沙运动。科学家们采用了一种多尺度分析方法，将高分辨率卫星图像与长期卫星观测相结合。他们分析了 2025 年 5 月至 8 月期间获取的四张北京三号卫星图像，每张图像的空间分辨率均为 1.2 米。这些图像使他们能够识别太阳能电池板，并使用根据红色和近红外反射率计算的归一化植被指数（NDVI）评估太阳能电池板之间生长的植被。研究人员手动绘制了太阳能电池板的地图，以将太阳能电池板覆盖的区域排除在植被分析之外。他们还使用空间分辨率为 30 米的 Landsat 卫星图像来跟踪 2008 年至 2025 年间的植被变化。
数据集通过 Google Earth Engine 进行处理，生成年度最大 NDVI 测量值。为了评估植被差异，研究小组将太阳能发电厂内的条件与延伸至发电厂边界外 120 米的邻近控制区域的条件进行了比较。排除与邻近光伏装置重叠的区域，仅保留大于 500 平方米的控制区域，以确保可靠的比较。研究人员还使用覆盖 2024 年至 2026 年的 Landsat 图像检查了 5 月至 8 月的每月植被变化。为了最大限度地减少太阳能电池板对低分辨率 Landsat 图像的干扰，他们开发了一种基于电池板覆盖范围的过滤方法。他们测试了 30% 到 70% 之间的五个覆盖阈值，以评估它们对 NDVI 测量的影响。为了进行长期分析，他们保留了太阳能电池板覆盖率不超过 50% 的像素。然后根据每个工厂的建设年份对植被记录进行调整，使研究人员能够检查从安装前五年到安装后十年的变化。由于施工前和施工后观察不足，2021 年、2024 年和 2025 年安装的电厂被排除在本次分析之外。
对 2025 年 158 个光伏电站站点的分析表明，电站内的植被始终比周边地区更绿，电站内的平均 NDVI 值比邻近对照区域高 11.5%，其中 8 月份记录的差异最大。 2024 年至 2026 年的 Landsat 观测在所有 12 个月的比较中证实了这一模式，NDVI 差异范围为 3.5% 至 10.7%。长期卫星数据还显示，光伏建设后植被条件持续改善。研究人员发现，安装后第二年，NDVI 就比施工前水平高出 19.9%，第二年到第五年平均高出 28.4%。 2013年至2018年期间竣工的工厂

【原文 English Original】
Researchers at China’s Hohai University have examined seasonal vegetation changes at the 21 GW Gonghe Talatan solar power cluster in Gonghe County, Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai province, China, and have found that vegetation levels surpassed pre-construction levels within two years of PV installation. The region is characterized by predominantly flat terrain at an average elevation of approximately 2,920 meters and a cold, arid to semi-arid climate. Average annual temperatures stand at 4.1 C, while annual precipitation reaches 303 mm, nearly 88% of which falls between May and September. Annual evaporation amounts to approximately 1,800 mm, while the region receives more than 2,900 hours of sunshine per year and experiences significant wind-driven sand movement. The scientists used a multiscale analytical approach combining high-resolution satellite imagery with long-term satellite observations. They analyzed four Beijing-3 satellite images acquired between May and August 2025, each with a spatial resolution of 1.2 meters. The images enabled them to identify solar panels and assess vegetation growing between them using the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), calculated from red and near-infrared reflectance. The researchers manually mapped the solar panels to exclude panel-covered areas from the vegetation analysis. They also used Landsat satellite imagery with a spatial resolution of 30 meters to track vegetation changes between 2008 and 2025. The datasets were processed through Google Earth Engine to generate annual maximum NDVI measurements. To assess vegetation differences, the team compared conditions within the solar plants with those in adjacent control areas extending up to 120 meters beyond the plant boundaries. Areas overlapping with neighboring PV installations were excluded, while only control areas larger than 500 square meters were retained to ensure reliable comparisons. The researchers also examined monthly vegetation changes from May to August using Landsat imagery covering 2024 to 2026. To minimize interference from solar panels in the lower-resolution Landsat images, they developed a filtering method based on panel coverage. They tested five coverage thresholds ranging from 30% to 70% to assess their influence on NDVI measurements. For the long-term analysis, they retained pixels with solar panel coverage of 50% or less. Vegetation records were then aligned according to each plant’s construction year, enabling the researchers to examine changes from five years before installation to 10 years afterward. Plants installed in 2021, 2024, and 2025 were excluded from this analysis because of insufficient pre- and post-construction observations. The analysis of 158 PV plant sites in 2025 showed that vegetation within the installations was consistently greener than in surrounding areas, with average NDVI values within the plants being 11.5% higher than in adjacent control areas, with the largest difference recorded in August. Landsat observations from 2024 to 2026 confirmed this pattern across all 12 monthly comparisons, with NDVI differences ranging from 3.5% to 10.7%. Long-term satellite data also revealed sustained improvements in vegetation conditions following PV construction. The researchers found that NDVI exceeded pre-construction levels by 19.9% in the second year after installation and was, on average, 28.4% higher between the second and fifth years. Plants completed between 2013 and 2018 recorded increases ranging from 14.1% to 35.9%, with older installations generally showing stronger vegetation recovery. “Generally, the NDVI within the PV plant polygons was slightly higher than that in the surrounding external areas,” the researchers explained. “This difference was particularly observed in the southern PV plant polygons, where vegetation greenness was obviously higher than that observed in the other PV plant polygons.” The researchers suggested that panel shading, reduced evaporation, lower wind speeds and rainfall redistribution could contribute to improved growing conditions. Water from panel cleaning and vegetation reseeding may also play a role, although these mechanisms were not directly verified. They cautioned that climatic variability, uncertainties associated with satellite measurements and the lack of field observations limit the findings, which may not be directly applicable to regions with different environmental conditions. Their findings are presented in the study “ Impacts of large-scale centralized photovoltaic plant construction on vegetation: Satellite evidence from Gonghe photovoltaic park, China ,” published in Information Geography . Previous research has also highlighted the potential environmental benefits of large-scale PV installations in arid regions. In October 2024, scientists at China’s Xi’an University of Technology examined the ecological effects of a 1 GW solar installation at the Qinghai Gonghe Photovoltaic Park. They found that the installation achieved a higher environmental assessment score than surrounding areas, suggesting improvements in local microclimate conditions, soil properties, and plant and microbial diversity. More recently, researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences examined the cooling effects of eight solar plants in China’s arid regions. They found that PV installations can create localized cooling effects extending between 120 meters and 540 meters beyond their boundaries, with cooling intensity reaching 3.1 C in some locations. Vegetation responses varied depending on seasonal conditions, geographical location and plant design, suggesting that the ecological benefits of large-scale solar development are strongly site-dependent. title: 特朗普訪華之際 美國封堵中國公司在東南亞租用AI算力的「後門」
summary: 特朗普訪華之際 美國封堵中國公司在東南亞租用AI算力的「後門」 - BBC News 中文 特朗普開啟亞洲之行的同時，美國商務部工業與安全局（BIS）週一（11月16日）發佈新規，要求向印尼、馬來西亞、新加坡、泰國和巴西出口、再出口或在境內轉移先進AI芯片時須申請美國許可。 新規還規定，總部或最終母公司位於中國及其他受美國武器禁運國家的企業，若通過海外數據中心租用大規模美國算力，同樣納入管制範圍。 此前，雖然美國限制最先進英偉達芯片直接銷往中國，但中國大型互聯網公司和AI實驗
content:
特朗普訪華之際 美國封堵中國公司在東南亞租用AI算力的「後門」 - BBC News 中文
特朗普開啟亞洲之行的同時，美國商務部工業與安全局（BIS）週一（11月16日）發佈新規，要求向印尼、馬來西亞、新加坡、泰國和巴西出口、再出口或在境內轉移先進AI芯片時須申請美國許可。
新規還規定，總部或最終母公司位於中國及其他受美國武器禁運國家的企業，若通過海外數據中心租用大規模美國算力，同樣納入管制範圍。
此前，雖然美國限制最先進英偉達芯片直接銷往中國，但中國大型互聯網公司和AI實驗室可以「只租算力、不買硬件」，即芯片部署在第三國數據中心，中國企業再通過互聯網遠程調用算力訓練模型，而無須把相關硬件運入中國。
但黃仁勳不久前因媒體報道他與Megaspeed前高管黃樂存在婚外情而辭職；Megaspeed既是英偉達的合作夥伴，也因可能把受管制芯片輸往中國而受到美國當局審查。
中國外交部批評新規是「經濟脅迫」，表示北京「將採取必要措施，堅定維護自身合法權益」。
按照此前的監管框架，只要芯片沒有實際出口或再出口到中國，遠程使用算力未必直接違反美國的芯片出口管制。
這讓東南亞、日本及其他地區的大型數據中心成為中國AI研發的重要外部算力來源之一。
CNBC報道，字節跳動、阿里巴巴和騰訊等中國公司，都曾通過馬來西亞、泰國和日本等地的數據中心遠程使用英偉達芯片。
這些交易通常不會直接以中國母公司的名義簽約，而是借助離岸架構、地區子公司或本地代理商完成。
華盛頓智庫進步研究所（Institute for Progress）此前估計，到2027年，中國至少有30%的先進AI算力可能來自海外數據中心租賃及東南亞地區的芯片走私。這一比例顯示，遠程算力已經不再只是硬件禁運之外的補充渠道，而是部分中國AI公司訓練大模型的重要支柱。
圖像加註文字，黃仁勳因媒體報道他與Megaspeed前高管黃樂存在婚外情而辭職；Megaspeed既是英偉達的合作夥伴，也因可能把受管制芯片輸往中國而受到美國當局審查。
新規規定，無論數據中心位於哪個國家，只要經營實體知道或有理由知道，其客戶或客戶的最終母公司位於中國、中國澳門及其他受美國武器禁運的國家，且提供的算力達到規定門檻，相關芯片供應便須接受許可審查。
按照新規，這一門檻是「總計TPP」（即總處理性能）超過1200萬。摩根士丹利估算，這一規模約相當於700至800塊英偉達H100芯片，而訓練大型模型往往需要數千乃至上萬塊同類先進芯片。這意味著，絕大多數用於大模型訓練的海外算力集群，都會落入許可審查範圍。
不僅如此，新規還列出了五個被視為轉口風險較高的國家，即印尼、馬來西亞、新加坡、泰國和巴西。換言之，即使最終用戶並非中國企業，單純向這五個國家轉運先進芯片，同樣需要申請美國出口許可。
摩根士丹利認為，BIS正從遠程訪問、芯片出貨和代工合規三個方向同步收緊中國取得先進算力的渠道，對中國互聯網和AI產業整體偏負面。該行稱新規較其先前預期「更為鷹派」，會增加阿里巴巴的下行風險；不過，阿里旗下自研芯片公司「平頭哥」的供應能見度較高，仍可能是阿里相對同業緩解衝擊的關鍵競爭優勢。
澳洲伊迪斯科文大學（Edith Cowan University）的國際貿易專家麥克多納（Naoise McDonagh）表示，馬來西亞和泰國等國的數據中心建設高度依賴中國買家，可能受創最重。但諮詢公司Verisk Maplecroft的Reema Bhattacharya認為，新規不太可能令整個數據中心熱潮脫軌，由大型科技企業支持、客戶身份明確的投資應「保持相對韌性」。
圖像加註文字，美國商務部長盧特尼克在黃仁勳事件後收到指責，並將接受美國國會的質詢。
新規發佈之際，正值美國總統特朗普前往中國與中國國家主席習近平會晤，也發生在英偉達前首席執行官黃仁勳辭職引發的政治風波之後。黃仁勳此前因媒體報道他與Megaspeed前高管黃樂存在婚外情而辭職；Megaspeed既是英偉達的合作夥伴，也因可能把受管制芯片輸往中國而受到美國當局審查。
發佈新規的BIS，雖隸屬商務部，但在聲明中罕見地說明，新規由財政部和白宮國家安全委員會撰寫並指示發佈。
美國財政部長斯科特·貝森特（Scott Bessent）在此前表示，財政部、五角大樓、國務院和美國貿易代表辦公室數月來都支持把Megaspeed列入貿易黑名單，但掌管名單的商務部並不贊成。貝森特形容，政府內部在處理該問題時存在「不同觀點」。
美國參議院商務委員會資深民主黨成員瑪麗亞·坎特韋爾（Maria Cantwell）在11月15日寫給盧特尼克的信中表示：「如果負責保護這一優勢的機構連自己的管制措施都不執行，美國就無法保持在人工智能領域的領導地位。」她指責商務部無視反覆出現的國家安全警告，並認為盧特尼克未能行使職權，「已經損害美國國家安全」。
坎特韋爾還提到，商務部曾在調查Megaspeed期間暫停行政調查，當時司法部要求把案件移交刑事調查。她批評商務部暫停調查後，沒有同時限制Megaspeed繼續取得先進AI芯片。
她還針對特朗普政府對部分銷往中國的英偉達芯片收取25%費用的安排提出質疑，認為這可能造成批准敏感技術出口的「反常財務誘因」，並令人質疑商務部是否將商業利益置於國家安全之上。
對於黃仁勳事件，中國否認相關指控。Megaspeed也未被認定違反美國規定，該公司表示，黃樂已於2025年8月離職，公司經營合法合規，並遵守美國出口管制要求。美國商務部發言人則拒絕對坎特韋爾的信作出評論。

content:
日本富岳超级计算机在网络攻击后下线
日本富岳超级计算机在网络攻击后下线
日本富岳超级计算机在网络攻击后下线
日本理化学研究所计算科学中心运营的富岳超级计算机因安全漏洞而下线。
该组织表示，11 月 10 日至 13 日期间，未经授权的一方利用显示 Fugaku 运行状态的公共仪表板来访问多个内部服务器。
尽管研究中心尚未确定访问方式，但 RIKEN 的调查证实，入侵者访问了一些服务器，植入了针对用户数据的恶意软件。
具体来说，该组织表示以下细节已被泄露：
4,222 位 Fugaku 用户的姓名、电子邮件地址和用户 ID
375 位 Rikyu 用户的姓名和电子邮件地址
SSH私钥和访问密钥存储在用户计算机上
研究存储在用户计算机上的数据文件
RIKEN指出，攻击者使用了一些访问密钥来尝试连接到其他系统，但调查并未确定进一步的未经授权的访问或盗窃研究结果。
该组织尚未确定此次攻击的来源，并且仍在努力确定确切的入侵方法。
RIKEN 计算科学中心运营着两台超级计算机，供学术界和工业界的研究人员使用。
Fugaku 于 2021 年 3 月开始共享使用，是一台 537 petaflops 超级计算机，用于药物发现、恶劣天气预报和空气传播病毒传播模拟。 Rikyu 是一台用于人工智能科学研究的 64 petaflops 超级计算机。
为了应对这一事件，RIKEN 于 11 月 14 日关闭了 Fugaku，禁用了用户的登录密钥，并要求用户撤销和替换他们存储在超级计算机上的所有凭据。
RIKEN 表示，富岳的运营只有在确保安全后才会恢复。
修复工作包括解决被利用的软件漏洞、重建受损服务器、检查网络配置以及实施先进的人工智能驱动的安全措施。
建议用户撤销 Fugaku 上存储的任何 SSH 密钥和其他凭据，并留意冒充 RIKEN 的可疑电子邮件。
RIKEN 发言人告诉 BleepingComputer，他们当时没有关于该事件的更多细节可透露，但承诺在调查发现新结果时发布最新信息。

Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offlline after cyberattack
Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offlline after cyberattack
Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offlline after cyberattack
The Fugaku supercomputer operated by Japan's RIKEN Center for Computational Science has been taken offline following a security breach.
The organization says that between November 10 and 13, an unauthorized party exploited the public dashboard displaying Fugaku's operational status to gain access to multiple internal servers.
Although the research center has yet to determine the access method, RIKEN’s investigation confirmed that the intruder accessed some servers to plant malware that targeted user data.
Specifically, the organization says that the following details have been compromised:
Names, email addresses, and user IDs of 4,222 Fugaku users
Names and email addresses of 375 Rikyu users
SSH private keys and access keys stored on users’ computers
Research data files stored on users’ computers
RIKEN notes that the attacker used some of the access keys in attempts to connect to additional systems, but the investigation did not determine further unauthorized access or theft of research results.
The organization has not attributed the attack, and it’s still working to determine the exact intrusion method.
RIKEN’s Center for Computational Science operates the two supercomputers, making them available to researchers in academia and industry sectors.
Fugaku, which entered shared use in March 2021, is a 537 petaflops supercomputer used in drug discovery, severe-weather forecasting, and simulations of airborne virus transmission. Rikyu is a 64 petaflops supercomputer used in AI scientific research.
In response to the incident, RIKEN shut down Fugaku on November 14, disabled users’ login keys, and asked users to revoke and replace any credentials they had stored on the supercomputer.
RIKEN said Fugaku operations will resume only after it has ensured that it’s safe to do so.
The remediation effort includes addressing the exploited software vulnerability, rebuilding compromised servers, reviewing the network configuration, and implementing advanced AI-driven security measures.
Users are advised to revoke any SSH keys and other credentials stored on Fugaku, and watch out for suspicious emails impersonating RIKEN.
A RIKEN spokesperson told BleepingComputer that they have no more details to share about the incident at the time, but promised to publish updates when the investigation uncovers new findings.

17 November 2026
